jahmyr gibbs.verdict: High volume + elite efficiency and extreme solo-back splits make him the overall 1.01 target
jahmyr gibbs.report: High volume plus elite efficiency: 21.6 PPG two straight years, 5.0 YPC, 84 first downs, and extreme solo-back splits (27+ PPG without Montgomery) with Pacheco now the only real backfield mate. Ceiling is the overall RB1. Floor risk is the contract hold-in—zero camp reps as of Aug 5 plus a flagged back issue—but Bijan's new deal should force resolution. Playoff slate @MIN, NYG, @CHI is fine.

bijan robinson.verdict: Paid, holdout resolved, every-down bell cow with strong receiving efficiency—cleanest RB1 profile
bijan robinson.report: Every-down workhorse: 287 carries, 103 targets, 78% snaps, 19.8% target share, WOPR 0.31—high volume with strong receiving efficiency (rec EPA 1.56). His new record extension removes holdout risk. Ceiling is overall RB1; the bell-cow usage anchors a high floor even in a middling offense. Only the gradual practice ramp-up is a mild concern. Playoffs @WSH, TB, NO are soft.

christian mccaffrey.verdict: Historic 2025 with elite receiving volume, but age-30 mileage and 2024 injury keep the floor honest
christian mccaffrey.report: 2025 was a historic bounce-back: 24.5 PPG, 23.4% target share, WOPR 0.40—elite volume and receiving, the high-volume/high-efficiency profile. But 2024 was wiped out by injury and he enters age-30 on nine years of wear, so the floor carries real games-missed risk. When healthy he's the positional 1a; the question is games played, not talent. Playoffs @LAC, @KC, PHI are tough.

jonathan taylor.verdict: Bell-cow rusher with rare positive rush EPA, but thin passing role and 320+ touch mileage cap him
jonathan taylor.report: Bell-cow rusher: 323 carries, +1.10 rush EPA/g, 27 broken tackles, 4.9 YPC—high volume with genuinely good ground efficiency at that load. Risks: back-to-back 320+ touch seasons invite regression/injury, an 11% target share caps his PPR ceiling, and production leaned on Daniel Jones staying upright. Solid RB1 floor, capped ceiling. Playoffs @TEN, CIN, @CLE are neutral.

de'von achane.verdict: High volume plus explosive efficiency and heavy receiving role give a PPR-proof floor and top-5 ceiling
de'von achane.report: High volume with strong efficiency: 5.7 YPC, 18.8% target share, 3.0 yards after contact, 22 broken tackles over 16 games. Elite receiving usage gives a PPR-proof floor; ceiling is a top-5 finish if Miami's offense clicks. Mild concern is that rec EPA dipped negative and he carries some injury variance on a smaller frame. Backfield is his—Wright/Gordon are depth. Playoffs @GB, LAC, BUF mixed.

james cook iii.verdict: Locked-in rushing volume but heavily TD-fueled scoring and a thin 40-target receiving role
james cook iii.report: High-volume rusher (309 carries) whose fantasy value is heavily TD-fueled—40 targets is a thin receiving role, and 7.55 pts/tgt reflects scoring on low volume rather than sticky usage. Buffalo's offense keeps the ceiling alive, but repeating a big TD count is hard to bank. Floor is fine given locked-in early-down and goal-line work. Playoffs CHI, @DEN, @MIA are workable.

jeremiyah love.verdict: Talented rookie but an unsettled three-way Arizona muddle makes the RB13 price too rich
jeremiyah love.report: Rookie with hype but no NFL data and a three-way muddle—alternating first-team reps with Allgeier while Benson returns from a knee injury and Conner lurks. His talent and receiving upside give a real ceiling if he seizes the job, but paying an RB1-range price for an unsettled committee role is steep. Floor is bench-level if he opens in a timeshare.

ashton jeanty.verdict: Heavy volume but the warning quadrant—dreadful rush efficiency needs Kubiak's scheme to unlock it
ashton jeanty.report: The warning quadrant: heavy volume (266 carries, 73 targets, 78% snaps) but ugly efficiency—3.7 YPC, -3.83 rush EPA/g, just 1.6 yards before contact behind a poor line. Kubiak's zone scheme is the bull case and could unlock the talent. Volume alone secures the floor; efficiency must rebound for the ceiling. Playoffs DEN, TEN, @ARI are fine.

omarion hampton.verdict: Three-down breakout profile if healthy, but 2025 injury and Keaton Mitchell cap the confidence
omarion hampton.report: Breakout profile with proven flashes—63% snaps and receiving chops (32 rec) on a 9-game sample. The LAC lead role gives three-down upside, but he missed 6+ games in 2025 and Keaton Mitchell adds explosive-play competition. Ceiling is a low-end RB1 across a full 17; floor reflects the games-missed and committee risk. Playoffs SF, @MIA, KC are mixed.

saquon barkley.verdict: 2024 spike regressed hard in 2025; big volume holds the floor but the ceiling needs efficiency back
saquon barkley.report: Cratered from 20.9 PPG (2024) to 13.7 (2025) with -1.51 rush EPA/g and 4.1 YPC—the 2024 TD/efficiency spike regressed hard while volume stayed. Age and mileage make a full rebound uncertain, though 280 carries in a strong offense holds the floor. Ceiling requires the efficiency to return. Playoffs SEA, HOU, @SF are neutral.

derrick henry.verdict: Age-32 anomaly still rushing well, but pure-TD profile and the ever-present clock cap the case
derrick henry.report: Age-32 anomaly still producing—5.2 YPC, 16 TDs—but the profile is pure rushing and TD-driven (4.9% target share, 0.07 WOPR, 55% snaps with Justice Hill on passing downs). He's one bad-luck season from collapse and the every-year clock is real. Ceiling is RB1 in a good offense; floor is exposed if TDs regress. Playoffs @PIT, CLE, @CIN.

chase brown.verdict: Steady three-down back with a strong receiving floor—ceiling and floor both hinge on Burrow's health
chase brown.report: Steady three-down back—88 targets, 14.3% target share, low 7.1 weekly stdev, 16.6 PPG. The receiving floor is strong; the swing factor is Burrow's health, with the data showing ~21 PPG when Burrow plays. Ceiling is a locked-in RB1 alongside an elite QB; floor sags if Burrow misses time again. Perine is minor competition. Playoffs @CAR, @IND, BAL are favorable.

kenneth walker iii.verdict: Team change to KC is the upgrade—TD environment jumps, but efficiency and pass-down role are open
kenneth walker iii.report: The move to Kansas City is the story—projected lead back in a high-scoring offense, a clear TD-environment upgrade from Seattle's 47%-snap committee. Efficiency has been middling (-0.84 rush EPA/g) and he's never been a true workhorse, so touch volume and the pass-down role are open questions. Ceiling is TD-fueled RB1 weeks; floor is committee. Discount any pre-trade ranks.

josh jacobs.verdict: Fading trusty vet propped up by goal-line TDs in a committee-leaning Green Bay backfield
josh jacobs.report: Trusty veteran fading—17.2 to 13.9 PPG, -0.99 rush EPA/g, 4.0 YPC—propped up by goal-line TDs in Green Bay's committee-leaning backfield. Volume (234 carries) and the scoring role keep an RB2 floor. Ceiling needs the TD rate to hold and health across 17. Playoffs MIA, @CHI, HOU are fine.

breece hall.verdict: Committee erosion cut his 2025, but receiving chops and an improved Jets offense keep bounce-back live
breece hall.report: Split-backfield risk—slipped to 12.2 PPG with Braelon Allen carving into the workload and -1.39 rush EPA/g. Receiving ability (48 targets) and a reportedly improved Jets offense give bounce-back upside. Ceiling is a return to the RB1 form he's already hit on this team; floor is committee frustration. Playoffs @ARI, NE, MIN are neutral.

javonte williams.verdict: Dallas rebound looked good, but low yds/tgt screams TD reliance and rookie Blue threatens the role
javonte williams.report: Rebound year in Dallas—14.3 PPG, 25 broken tackles, 2.4 yards after contact, positive rush EPA—but value leaned on TDs (2.7 yds/tgt is alarmingly low) and rookie Jaydon Blue threatens the passing-down role. Strip his injury-shortened weeks and the PPG reads RB1-ish. Floor is committee; ceiling is low-end RB1 if he holds volume. Playoffs @LAR, JAX, NYG.

kyren williams.verdict: Efficient and safe, but shrinking touch and goal-line share to Corum threatens the TD-based value
kyren williams.report: Efficient, low-variance producer (15.5 PPG, 5.9 stdev), but the usage arrow points down—touch share dropped 78%→58% after Week 7 and goal-line share ceded to Corum (74%→53%). That's bell-cow-to-committee, which undercuts a TD-dependent scoring base. Floor is a safe-ish RB2; ceiling is capped by the shrinking role. Playoffs DAL, @SEA, @TB.

travis etienne jr..verdict: Pass-catching rebound, but TD-fueled value plus a downgraded offense make me pass on the sleeper tag
travis etienne jr..report: Bounce-back to 14.9 PPG, but the analysis flags it as TD-fueled and he now moves from a top offense to a bottom-tier New Orleans unit with Kamara still around. ESPN tagged him a sleeper as a pass-catcher in an 'improved' offense, but at an inside-top-100 price with the offense downgraded I skip the badge. Floor is RB2; ceiling capped by scheme. Playoffs @TB, ARI, @ATL.

cam skattebo.verdict: Year-2 breakout bet with a three-down role, but weak efficiency and a crowded backfield temper it
cam skattebo.report: Year-2 breakout bet—flashed a 12.9% target share and 1.02 pts/touch as a rookie, but efficiency was poor (-1.51 rush EPA/g) on a weak Giants offense, and Tracy/Singletary crowd the backfield. ESPN's opportunity call is real, but at an inside-top-100 ADP he's not a true sleeper. Ceiling is RB2 with a three-down role; floor is committee. Playoffs CLE, @DET, @DAL.

quinshon judkins.verdict: Poor per-touch data and a Sampson timeshare on a weak offense cap him at flex-plus
quinshon judkins.report: Poor-efficiency committee back—3.6 YPC, -1.79 rush EPA/g, only 1.4 yards before contact behind a bad line, splitting snaps (51%) with Dylan Sampson. Cleveland's weak offense caps the scoring environment. Volume could grow, but the per-touch data is a red flag. Floor is flex; ceiling is low-end RB2 if he wins the job outright. Playoffs @NYG, @BAL, IND are tough.

bucky irving.verdict: 2024 RB1 line proves the ceiling; 2025 was injury-wrecked, and healthy he's a high-volume, high-efficiency back
bucky irving.report: Irving's 2024 (14.4 ppg, 5.4 ypc, 0.96 pts/touch) is the true talent; 2025's 8.1 ppg and -3.56 rush EPA/g came in a broken offense across only ~10 healthy games. He's the clear TB1 (62% snaps) but Gainwell devoured targets while he sat, capping his receiving share. High-volume/good-efficiency profile when right — ceiling is a return to RB1. Floor is another injury year in a split. Playoff slate (NO, @ATL, LAR) is fine.

treveyon henderson.verdict: Efficient rookie (5.1 ypc, 3.0 ybc/rush) but only 46% snaps and faded once Stevenson returned
treveyon henderson.report: Henderson posted strong per-touch efficiency as a rookie (5.1 ypc, 3.0 yards before contact, 0.96 pts/touch) but at just a 46% snap share in a genuine committee. The Smyth flag is real: under 10 ppg over his last nine once Stevenson was healthy, and camp chatter questions his pass-blocking, which gates third-down work. Low-volume/good-efficiency — a breakout only if he seizes the job. Floor is a frustrating timeshare; tough wk15 @KC.

bhayshul tuten.verdict: Explosive talent but 2025 was a 21%-snap, 3.7-ypc committee sliver in a crowded JAX room
bhayshul tuten.report: Tuten barely played (21% snaps, 83 carries, 5 broken tackles) and his 3.7 ypc with -0.68 rush EPA/g doesn't yet show efficiency to force volume. Low-volume/mediocre-efficiency, though the receiving points/target flashes. He nominally leads a muddy depth chart (Rodriguez, Allen, Abdullah) but has commanded nothing. Ceiling is a lead-back leap if he separates in camp; floor is a rotational dart. ADP inside the top 100 makes him no bargain.

d'andre swift.verdict: Genuine three-down workhorse (223 car, 58% snaps) with rising rush EPA and a steady, low-variance floor
d'andre swift.report: Swift quietly improved to 13.4 ppg with 223 carries, 4.9 ypc and +0.97 rush EPA/g, plus a low 7.1 weekly stdev — high-volume with now-adequate efficiency. Monangai eats into early-down work but has no receiving role, so Swift owns passing downs and the target floor that PPR rewards. Ceiling is a low-end RB1; floor is a dependable RB2. Playoff draw is rough (@BUF, GB, DET).

david montgomery.verdict: New team, 37% snaps and TD-reliant; the 2024 RB2 line masks shrinking usage behind Woody Marks
david montgomery.report: Montgomery slid to 9.8 ppg on a 37% snap share with just 24 receptions — high per-touch value (0.92 pts/touch) but a volume profile that leans hard on goal-line scores. Moving to Houston with Woody Marks pushing for the receiving/change-up role, his floor is fragile if TDs regress. High-efficiency/low-volume in a committee. Ceiling needs him to hold the early-down and goal-line lion's share; wk16 @PHI is a tough playoff spot.

jadarian price.verdict: Buzzy Hard Knocks rookie (6.0 ypc, 13 college TDs) genuinely pushing Charbonnet for the SEA job
jadarian price.report: No NFL data, but the checkable camp signal is strong: multiple Hard Knocks/beat reports of first-team reps and power/explosion, plus ESPN's sleeper call on his 6.0 ypc college profile. He's competing with Charbonnet and Wilson, so the range is wide. Ceiling is a rookie who wins a lead role in a good offense; floor is a committee back who loses the camp battle. ADP just inside the top 100, so priced closer to the buzz than a true steal.

tony pollard.verdict: Durable 242-carry workhorse but poor efficiency (-1.28 rush EPA/g) makes the volume itself a risk at 29
tony pollard.report: Pollard's back-to-back near-1,100-yard seasons ride volume (242 carries, 62% snaps) not efficiency — -1.28 rush EPA/g and only 28 carries inside the 10 signal touchdown scarcity. High-volume/poor-efficiency is the warning quadrant: the workload is TD-light and Spears/Singleton lurk. Age 29 with heavy mileage adds decline risk. Low 5.5 stdev gives a stable RB2 floor; ceiling is capped without more goal-line work.

jaylen warren.verdict: Broke out to 12.8 ppg with elite tackle-breaking, but Dowdle's arrival flips him to a true committee
jaylen warren.report: Warren's 2025 was a real leap — 217 pts, 4.5 ypc, 23 broken tackles and +0.67 rec EPA/g on a 51% snap share — high-volume/good-efficiency. But he's now listed behind Rico Dowdle in Pittsburgh, turning last year's near-lead role into a split that caps both. His receiving chops (40 catches) preserve a PPR floor. Ceiling if he wins the job outright; floor a frustrating timeshare. Priced right outside the top 100.

rhamondre stevenson.verdict: Efficient (1.10 pts/touch, +0.94 rec EPA/g) but boom-bust and now the clear #2 to Henderson
rhamondre stevenson.report: Stevenson stayed productive (10.5 ppg, 1.10 pts/touch, 16 broken tackles, +0.94 rec EPA/g) even sharing time, but a huge 10.0 weekly stdev screams volatility and he's now behind Henderson on the depth chart. His WOPR 0.18 and 4.3 aDOT show real passing-game usage — a legit PPR outlet. Ceiling if Henderson's pass-block issues keep Stevenson on third downs; floor is a low-snap committee back. Tough wk15 @KC.

rico dowdle.verdict: Two straight ~230-carry, 12+ ppg seasons; new team but a proven volume back leading the PIT room
rico dowdle.report: Dowdle has back-to-back workhorse lines (236 carries, 56% snaps, 39 catches, 12.7 ppg) with steady if unspectacular efficiency (4.6 ypc, ~0.14 WOPR). Moving to Pittsburgh he's the listed lead, but Warren's tackle-breaking and receiving make it a live split. High-volume/average-efficiency; the target work supports a PPR floor. Ceiling if he holds 230+ touches; floor a near-even committee. Value right outside the top 100.

kenny gainwell.verdict: League-winning pass-game usage (16.3% tgt share, 73 rec) when Bucky sat; a PPR handcuff with standalone value
kenny gainwell.report: Gainwell's 2025 was volume-driven receiving gold — 85 targets, 73 catches, 16.3% target share, 0.23 WOPR, 13.0 ppg with 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on. That share collapses with a healthy Irving, but his pass-catching role and Bucky's injury history give real standalone/insurance value. Low rush efficiency means he needs targets to score. Start taking him around round 10 as the RB with a built-in PPR floor plus league-winning upside if Irving misses time.

chuba hubbard.verdict: 2024 RB1 line cratered to 7.4 ppg and 1 broken tackle; efficiency collapse plus Brooks returning is a fade
chuba hubbard.report: Hubbard's 2025 was ugly — 3.8 ypc, -1.04 rush EPA/g and a stunning 1 broken tackle on 134 carries after a strong 2024. High-volume-turned-inefficient, the classic sign the workload is at risk. Now Jonathon Brooks is back from injury and pushing for the job. Ceiling is a return to the 2024 form if he holds lead duties; floor is losing the backfield outright. Wk16 @PIT is a tough playoff draw.

aaron jones sr..verdict: 2024 stud, 2025 injury-and-efficiency crash (7.0 ppg, 2.90 pts/tgt); age and fade signals stack up
aaron jones sr..report: Jones fell from 14.2 ppg to 7.0 as efficiency (2.90 pts/target, 4.9 yds/tgt) and health both slipped. The talent gave a genuine RB1 line in 2024, but the trend and mileage point down, and the crowd is openly fading him. High-usage-when-healthy but the per-opportunity numbers no longer support it. Ceiling if the offense revives and he's healthy; floor is another injury-shortened, low-efficiency year.

rachaad white.verdict: Elite pass-pro/third-down back on a new team, but stuck behind Croskey-Merritt with a receiving-only path
rachaad white.report: White's calling card is passing-down work (40+ catches both years, 1.02 pts/touch in 2024) but his rushing efficiency is thin (4.8 yds/tgt, -2.3 aDOT) and 2025 dipped to 8.4 ppg. In Washington he's the listed #2 behind JCM, so his value is a receiving/two-minute role — a PPR floor without much rush ceiling. The Sanderson call is about pass-protection value, not a bell-cow projection, so I hold off the sleeper tag. Ceiling needs a JCM injury.

jonathon brooks.verdict: Cleared from knee recovery and buzzing in camp; the talent to overtake a fading Hubbard is real
jonathon brooks.report: No usable NFL data after the knee rehab, but ESPN flags he can overtake the starter and camp reports have him making noise — and Hubbard's 2025 collapse leaves the door open. The upside is a lead back in Carolina; the risk is a second serious knee injury and a slow ramp. Wide outcome range. Start taking the swing around round 11-12: the specific opening is Hubbard's -1.04 rush EPA/g decline, which makes this a genuine value if the knee holds.

j.k. dobbins.verdict: Efficient when upright (5.0 ypc) but a 10-game injury year again and a receiving void ceding work to Harvey
j.k. dobbins.report: Dobbins ran well (5.0 ypc, +0.42 rush EPA/g) but managed only 10 games and 14 targets — a rushing/TD-dependent profile with no receiving floor. New team Denver names him RB1, yet RJ Harvey owns the passing downs, capping ceiling and total touches. His own 'good for 10 weeks' line captures the risk. Ceiling is a healthy early-down/goal-line role; floor is another injury-shortened split.

rj harvey.verdict: Rookie with standout receiving efficiency (+1.12 rec EPA/g, 47 rec); Dobbins' injury history opens the door
rj harvey.report: Harvey posted 12.2 ppg and elite receiving value as a rookie — 58 targets, 47 catches, 0.15 WOPR, +1.12 rec EPA/g — on just a 42% snap share, the low-volume/high-efficiency breakout profile. He's the passing-down back to Dobbins, whose durability is shaky. Ceiling is a lead role if Dobbins misses time; floor is a change-of-pace with a PPR pulse. Start taking him around round 10 as the Denver back with the safer receiving floor and real upside.

kyle monangai.verdict: Efficient rookie runner (4.6 ypc), but no receiving role, second-half volume dip and missed practices temper the hype
kyle monangai.report: Monangai flashed on the ground (4.6 ypc, 3.0 yards before contact) but the Smyth data undercuts the ESPN 'expanding role' call: his volume actually fell once Swift returned and he has no receiving work (brick-hands reputation), which caps PPR upside. Chatter of three straight missed practices is a mild real concern. Low-volume/decent-rush-efficiency but role-locked behind Swift, so I skip the sleeper tag. Ceiling needs a Swift injury.

jacory croskey-merritt.verdict: Lead rusher in a good offense (175 car, 4.6 ypc, 13 broken tackles) at RB43 cost — cheap standalone value
jacory croskey-merritt.report: JCM ran efficiently as a rookie (4.6 ypc, 13 broken tackles, 8.3 ppg) and is the listed WSH RB1, but 13 targets all year means White siphons passing downs, making him a rush/TD-dependent, PPR-light profile. Low-volume/solid-rush-efficiency with a path to more carries. Start taking him around round 12: the opening is that he's the lead ground back at a deep-in-the-draft price. Floor is a two-man committee; ceiling a 250-touch runner.

blake corum.verdict: Efficient (5.1 ypc) but a pure handcuff with zero receiving value (72nd of 72 in YPRR) behind healthy Kyren
blake corum.report: Corum runs well on limited work (5.1 ypc, 3.5 yards before contact) but at a 29% snap share and dead last among RBs in yards per route run, he has no standalone or PPR value while Kyren Williams is upright. Low-volume/good-rush-but-no-receiving profile makes him almost purely a lottery-ticket handcuff. Ceiling is a Kyren injury unlocking a Rams lead role; floor is inactive fantasy weeks. Draft as insurance, not a starter.

woody marks.verdict: Real 196-carry volume in 2025 but ugly rushing efficiency flags the workload as fragile behind Montgomery.
woody marks.report: High-volume/poor-efficiency quadrant: 196 carries and 24 catches produced 151 pts, but rush EPA/g -1.82 and 3.6 ypc mean the touches, not the talent, carried him. Only 6.8% target share and 52% snaps. Montgomery sits ahead as RB1, capping the standalone role. Floor is a low-end flex; ceiling requires an injury bump. Playoff slate (@PHI, @GB) is rough.

zach charbonnet.verdict: On PUP after Feb ACL surgery with no timetable — injury torpedoes an otherwise decent committee profile.
zach charbonnet.report: The verified fact rules here: PUP recovering from February ACL surgery, no coaching-staff return date. That gutts games-played and caps 2026 regardless of his solid 2024-25 (181 pts, 0.89 pts/touch, 14 broken tackles). The stale FantasyPros sleeper call predates the surgery, so I skip it. If he returns midseason to a muddled backfield there's flex upside, but the floor is near-zero-usage risk.

jordan mason.verdict: Efficient bruiser (4.8 ypc, 2.3 YBC) a snap from a workhorse role if Aaron Jones misses time.
jordan mason.report: Low-volume/strong-efficiency profile with real thump: 159 carries, 4.8 ypc, 2.3 yds before contact, 13 broken tackles. Only 3.5% target share limits the PPR floor, but the rushing efficiency is legit and Aaron Jones' age/injury history makes the path obvious. That's the genuine opening — I'd start taking him in the 12th-13th round. Ceiling is a top-24 line if he inherits the backfield.

alvin kamara.verdict: Steep 2024→2025 collapse (15.6→5.9 ppg) with brutal EPA signals a back near the end.
alvin kamara.report: The forward read is decline: rush EPA/g -2.62 and rec EPA/g -1.06 in 2025, 3.6 ypc, and just 101 pts after a 265-pt 2024. Now age-33 range and slotted behind a younger starter. The RotoWire PPR-role call has some merit given his target history, but the efficiency data contradicts a rebound. Floor is a bench body; ceiling caps as a low-end flex if volume returns.

isiah pacheco.verdict: Buried behind Gibbs after a lost 2025; only a Gibbs injury unlocks any real value.
isiah pacheco.report: Efficiency cratered in 2025 (3.9 ypc, rush EPA/g -1.05, just 1 broken tackle) and he now sits as an RB2/3 behind Jahmyr Gibbs, one of the league's best. Low volume, low efficiency — a fade at cost unless the depth chart moves. The 'clear path to climb' sleeper framing overstates it with Gibbs entrenched. Contingent handcuff value only.

chris rodriguez jr..verdict: Positive rush EPA early-down grinder with zero pass game — pure contingent handcuff.
chris rodriguez jr..report: The one bright spot is efficient running: 4.5 ypc, rush EPA/g +0.52 on 112 carries. But 1.3% target share and no receiving role gut the PPR floor, and the 71-point projection reflects a backup snap count. Value is entirely tied to the back ahead of him getting hurt. TD-dependent, low ceiling in this format.

brian robinson jr..verdict: Collapsed to 17% snaps and now stuck behind Bijan — the sleeper call ignores the depth chart.
brian robinson jr..report: After 160 pts as WSH's lead back in 2024, he cratered to 63 pts on a 17% snap share in 2025 and lands behind Bijan Robinson, a workhorse who barely leaves the field. The staff-sleeper tag is a volume-dependent bet with no volume available. Efficiency is fine (2.6 YBC) but irrelevant without touches. Floor is near-empty; ceiling needs a Bijan injury.

tank bigsby.verdict: Elite per-carry efficiency (5.7 ypc, 3.0 YBC) trapped behind Saquon — no path to volume.
tank bigsby.report: Textbook low-volume/high-efficiency: 5.7 ypc, 3.0 yds before contact, 2.7 after in 2025, but only 13% snaps and 63 carries after the PHI trade. Saquon Barkley owns the workload, so the talent has nowhere to go. 1.2% target share means no PPR safety net. A pure Saquon handcuff whose ceiling only opens with an injury.

ray davis.verdict: RB4 on the Bills depth chart — efficient in spurts but too buried to matter.
ray davis.report: Solid touch efficiency (4.7 ypc, 0.94 pts/touch) and a decent 2024 flash, but he sits behind Cook, Ty Johnson and Gore at just a 14% snap share. Projection of 38 reflects reality: no standalone role. Would need multiple injuries ahead of him to reach flex relevance. Deep-stash only.

tyrone tracy jr..verdict: Proven dual-threat volume (176 car, 36 rec, 10.8% target share) mispriced at RB50-range ADP.
tyrone tracy jr..report: High-volume, average-efficiency lead-back profile: 161 pts, 54% snaps, 10.8% target share and a 0.16 WOPR — genuine three-down usage that PPR rewards. Rush EPA/g -0.65 is the flag, and rookie/committee competition could siphon carries, but the receiving floor is real. At ADP 167 the pass-game usage is the edge — I'd take him in the 13th round as a flex with RB2 upside.

mike washington jr..verdict: Rookie with no NFL usage data buried in a crowded Raiders backfield — dart throw.
mike washington jr..report: No 2024 or 2025 production to interpret, so opportunity is inferred from a modest 65-point projection and a depth chart that doesn't clear a path. Rookies with no defined role and starters ahead rarely return value in redraft. Ceiling exists only if injuries open touches; floor is a waiver drop. Pure speculation at this cost.

tyler allgeier.verdict: Steady committee back on a 'ride the hot hand' team behind a rookie lead and Conner.
tyler allgeier.report: Consistent low-variance grinder: 123 pts, 143 carries, 0.78 pts/touch, but only 30% snaps and 3.2% target share. New in ARI behind rookie Jeremiyah Love with James Conner also in the mix — LaFleur's hot-hand approach means touches aren't guaranteed. Efficiency is fine, not special; volume is the concern. Flex ceiling in the right week, bench floor otherwise.

dylan sampson.verdict: Rookie pass-catching niche (40 tgt, +0.46 rec EPA/g) gives a PPR floor behind Judkins.
dylan sampson.report: Low-volume/split profile but the receiving usage is real: 40 targets, 33 catches, 8.7% target share and a strong rec EPA/g +0.46, offsetting a bad 2.7 ypc. Judkins owns the early-down work, but Sampson's third-down role has PPR standalone value and expands if Judkins struggles. That receiving niche is the edge — worth a 14th-round flier for the catch floor.

tyjae spears.verdict: 12.3% target share receiving role and a 149-point projection well above his RB55-range ADP.
tyjae spears.report: The receiving usage carries him: 50 targets, 45 catches, 12.3% target share, 0.15 WOPR and a strong 0.95 pts/touch in a pass-catching role behind Pollard. ESPN's 149 projection versus ADP 168 flags a market gap the usage data supports. Rushing is inefficient (3.9 ypc) and he splits with Pollard, but the PPR floor is sturdy — a 12th-13th round value with upside if Pollard misses time.

braelon allen.verdict: Lost 2025 to injury; a power handcuff to Breece Hall with limited standalone touches.
braelon allen.report: Only 4 games and 15 pts in 2025 after an injury-shortened year, with a poor rush EPA/g -2.17 in that tiny sample. Behind Breece Hall, his path is contingent. The 2024 backup line (85 pts) shows a viable role exists if Hall misses time. Floor is a bench stash; ceiling is a startable early-down back only in an injury scenario.

keaton mitchell.verdict: Explosive per-carry (5.8 ypc, 3.6 YBC) but stuck behind rookie workhorse Omarion Hampton.
keaton mitchell.report: Elite big-play efficiency — 5.8 ypc, a huge 3.6 yds before contact — is the tantalizing part, but only 17% snaps and 59 carries. Omarion Hampton is the entrenched lead, so opportunity is the missing ingredient the 'need a chance' framing correctly identifies. Without volume it stays a spike-week dart; I'm not badging a player this buried. Ceiling needs a Hampton injury.

jordan james.verdict: Unproven CMC handcuff whose value lives entirely on McCaffrey's injury history.
jordan james.report: Essentially no NFL usage (2% snaps over 3 games) and currently listed Questionable himself, so opportunity is projection-only. The appeal is purely leverage on CMC's well-documented injury history — if McCaffrey misses time, whoever wins that backfield (James or Guerendo) is a smash. Too much uncertainty for a standalone bet; a lottery-ticket handcuff.

james conner.verdict: A zero-point projection screams season-ending injury — undraftable in redraft.
james conner.report: The 2026 projection of 0 combined with only 3 games in 2025 and a Questionable tag indicates he is not expected to play a meaningful role, likely an injury/IR situation. The 2024 workhorse line (254 pts) is irrelevant forward. Now buried at RB3 behind Love and Allgeier. The RotoWire 'would start elsewhere' call is contradicted by the projection — no badge, avoid.

justice hill.verdict: Pure receiving back (1.67 pts/touch) with a PPR floor and Henry-age contingency upside.
justice hill.report: Distinct pass-catching profile: 27 targets, 21 catches on just 18 carries, 10% target share and a huge 1.67 pts/touch. 2024's 42-catch season shows the ceiling of the role. Derrick Henry's age makes Hill's early-down bump plausible, adding to a receiving-driven PPR floor. That catch role at ADP 170 is the value — a 14th-round PPR dart with real weekly relevance.

jonah coleman.verdict: Rookie flagged by Smyth for Payton's RB pass usage; buried but with a clear injury path.
jonah coleman.report: No pro data yet, so it's a projection bet: Sean Payton's scheme feeds RBs in the passing game and Coleman lands as RB3 behind an injury-prone J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. The named Smyth/FantasyPros call and Dobbins' history give a plausible climb, which is the specific opening — worth a final-round stash. But the crowded room and 41-point projection keep the floor low; take him round 15+.

kaelon black.verdict: Third-string 49ers rookie, but James' rib injury and CMC's age make this backfield worth a late dart
kaelon black.report: No NFL data; pure projection. Quadrant unknown—he's an unproven rookie behind CMC (elite but aging) and Jordan James, who the chatter reports is missing camp with a rib injury (a checkable fact that nudges Black up the pecking order). Floor is near-zero standalone value as RB3. Ceiling requires two injuries ahead, but the 49ers backfield produces when opportunity opens. Tough wk16 @KC playoff draw. Handcuff lottery ticket only.

kaytron allen.verdict: Buried WSH rookie behind Croskey-Merritt, White and McNichols—no realistic path to volume
kaytron allen.report: No pro data to grade volume or efficiency; he's a projection-only rookie sitting fourth on a crowded depth chart. That competition (Croskey-Merritt starting, White and McNichols ahead) is the whole story—there's no opening. Floor is essentially waiver fodder. Ceiling needs multiple injuries and still shares work. Not a priority even in deep leagues.

nicholas singleton.verdict: Talented PSU rookie stuck behind Pollard and oft-injured Spears—real upside if the room thins
nicholas singleton.report: No NFL usage yet, so talent and situation drive the read. He's RB3 behind Pollard (the lead) and Spears, who has a lengthy injury history—a plausible path to a committee role exists. Floor is a low-touch rookie deep on the chart. Ceiling is a genuine flex if Spears misses time and Singleton earns the change-of-pace/passing role. At an ADP outside the top 150, I'd start taking him in the final rounds as a sleeper on the opening ahead of him.

demond claiborne.verdict: Vikings rookie behind aging Jones and Mason—handcuff upside but no current standalone role
demond claiborne.report: No pro data; projection-only rookie at RB3 behind Aaron Jones (aging) and Jordan Mason. The low-engagement 'breakout before the price catches up' chatter is vague hype with no camp specifics—ignore it. Floor is minimal touches. Ceiling opens only if Jones fades or gets hurt, and even then he shares with Mason. Speculative late-round stash.

kimani vidal.verdict: Flashed as a fill-in but 2025 efficiency was poor; now stuck behind Omarion Hampton
kimani vidal.report: His 118 points on 14 games came as an injury fill-in—high volume but poor per-carry efficiency (4.1 ypc, rush EPA/g -1.08, only 1.8 yards before contact). That's the warning quadrant: the volume itself was replaceable. Now he's RB3 behind Omarion Hampton. Floor is spot duty. Ceiling requires a Hampton injury, and even then his efficiency profile caps the payoff. Pure handcuff.

jaylen wright.verdict: Direct Achane handcuff with speed, but a tiny, inefficient role and Gordon competing behind him
jaylen wright.report: Low volume (22% snaps, 4.1% target share) and weak efficiency (rush EPA/g -0.63, negative air-yards share)—low-volume/poor-efficiency fade profile as things stand. He is, though, the nominal backup to injury-prone Achane, whose exit would flood one back with touches. Floor is minimal. Ceiling depends entirely on an Achane injury AND beating out Ollie Gordon for lead work. Contingent value only.

ollie gordon ii.verdict: Coach floated 'every-down' talk, but rookie efficiency was ugly; still an Achane contingency
ollie gordon ii.report: Rookie line shows poor efficiency—2.8 ypc, rush EPA/g -0.56, 1.8% target share—the low-volume/poor-efficiency zone. Hafley's 'can be an every-down back' quote is a real coach signal but reads as camp coachspeak, and Miami isn't a two-back offense. Floor is committee scraps. Ceiling is a lead role only if Achane (injury history) misses time and Gordon beats Wright. Late flier.

adam randall.verdict: Ravens rookie behind Derrick Henry and Justice Hill—no path barring injury
adam randall.report: No NFL data; projection-only rookie at RB3. Henry is the workhorse and Justice Hill owns passing downs, leaving nothing for Randall now. Floor is inactive/spot work. Ceiling needs a Henry injury and still likely splits with Hill. Late-season wk13 bye is fine but the role isn't there. Deep-stash only.

samaje perine.verdict: Reliable passing-down veteran behind Chase Brown, but capped low-ceiling role
samaje perine.report: Consistent low-variance receiving back—28 catches in 2024, 17 in 2025, but efficiency has slipped (2.33 to 3.71 pts/tgt going the wrong way as touches shifted). Clear low-volume role behind Chase Brown. Floor is steady PPR dribs; ceiling is limited unless Brown misses time. The proj-101 outlier isn't supported by his shrinking role. Bench depth in deep PPR only.

lequint allen jr..verdict: Low-usage Jaguars back with a modest pass-game role and thin standalone value
lequint allen jr..report: 2025 gave 25 points on tiny volume—2.1% target share, rush EPA/g -0.20, WOPR 0.03: low-volume, below-average efficiency. There's a sliver of receiving usage (10 catches) that could grow. Floor is negligible. Ceiling depends on an expanded role in a Jaguars backfield that isn't clearly settled. Speculative deep-league piece.

marshawn lloyd.verdict: Explosive on paper but injury-riddled; buried behind Josh Jacobs with no track record
marshawn lloyd.report: No usable NFL data—he's missed nearly his entire career to injuries, which is the dominant signal. He sits behind bell-cow Josh Jacobs. Floor is another lost/limited year. Ceiling is real burst if healthy and Jacobs misses time, but you're betting on availability he hasn't shown. Handcuff dart with elevated bust risk.

jaydon blue.verdict: Named in an ESPN 'need opportunity' piece, but rough rookie efficiency behind Javonte Williams
jaydon blue.report: Tiny sample (5 games, 26% snaps) with poor efficiency—3.4 ypc, rush EPA/g -1.50, 1.2 yards after contact: low-volume/poor-efficiency so far. The Bowen/Cockcroft 'skills, need a chance' mention is an opportunity call, but Javonte Williams is the entrenched starter and the data doesn't yet back a breakout. Floor minimal; ceiling is speed-back flex only if Williams exits. Late dart.

george holani.verdict: Fourth on Seattle's chart with 6% snaps—essentially undraftable outside the deepest leagues
george holani.report: 2025 was 15 points on a 6% snap share with poor rushing efficiency (3.3 ypc, rush EPA/g -0.93)—low-volume/poor-efficiency fade. He's buried at RB4 behind Price, Charbonnet and Wilson. Floor is inactive. Ceiling needs a cascade of injuries. No reason to draft in standard formats.

ty johnson.verdict: Efficient PPR receiving back with standalone value—underpriced for the pass-game role he owns
ty johnson.report: Two straight seasons near 100 points with elite per-touch efficiency (1.36 pts/touch, rec EPA/g 0.67, 8.0 yds/tgt)—the low-volume/strong-efficiency profile that already produces without needing an injury. He owns Buffalo's passing-down role behind Cook. Floor is a usable deep-league flex; ceiling climbs if Cook misses time. At an ADP outside the top 150 that receiving role is a genuine value—I'd start taking him in the final rounds.

emari demercado.verdict: Big-play efficiency on light volume, but stuck as a change-of-pace behind the starter
emari demercado.report: Explosive per-touch numbers—7.1 ypc, 4.4 yards before contact, 1.02 pts/touch—the low-volume/strong-efficiency zone, but that ypc screams TD/big-play variance rather than sustainable volume. He's a clear backup with a 23% snap share. Floor is spot work; ceiling opens only on an injury ahead of him. Efficient flier, not a bankable asset.

isaiah davis.verdict: Quietly efficient dual-threat behind Hall and Allen—flex upside if the Jets room thins
isaiah davis.report: 2025 improved to 71 points with solid receiving usage (6.3% target share, rec EPA/g 0.29, 5.5 ypc)—low-volume but genuinely good efficiency, the breakout-if-opportunity profile. The catch is a deep chart: Breece Hall and Braelon Allen are both ahead. Floor is limited touches; ceiling is a real flex if Hall misses time given Davis's receiving chops. Sensible late stash.

emmett johnson.verdict: Rookie third on the chart—no data and no clear path to touches
emmett johnson.report: No NFL usage to evaluate; projection-only rookie behind Walker and Demercado. The competition is the story—two backs entrenched ahead of him. Floor is inactive/spot work. Ceiling requires multiple injuries and even then he'd share. Watch-list stash, not a draft priority.

chris brooks.verdict: On PUP and buried behind Jacobs—minimal role even when healthy
chris brooks.report: Pass-catching profile but low efficiency (1.92 pts/tgt in 2025, rush EPA/g -0.29) and now on PUP, a real availability red flag. He's a distant backup to Josh Jacobs. Floor is missed time; ceiling is a small passing-down role at best. No standalone value to chase.

sean tucker.verdict: Explosive but volatile Irving handcuff—boom weeks exist, but he's third on the chart
sean tucker.report: 2025 gave 91 points but with huge weekly variance (stdev 8.0) and poor sustained efficiency (3.7 ypc, 1.0 yards after contact)—boom-bust on limited volume. The Bowen/Cockcroft 'need a chance' mention is an opportunity call, but he sits behind Irving and Gainwell. Floor is a few spike weeks; ceiling is a lead role only if Irving misses time. High-variance late dart.

dj giddens.verdict: Lone clear backup to workhorse Jonathan Taylor—the most valuable handcuff on this board
dj giddens.report: Tiny rookie sample, but the situation is what matters: he's the direct backup to Jonathan Taylor, a true workhorse whose absence would funnel a massive touch load to one back with little competition (only Seth McGowan behind). Floor is spot work while Taylor plays. Ceiling is RB1-adjacent volume if Taylor misses time. At an ADP outside the top 150, that contingent bell-cow path makes him a sleeper worth a final-round pick.

malik davis.verdict: Deep Dallas backup with 21% snaps and no receiving role; only matters if Javonte Williams goes down
malik davis.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency quadrant: 1.4% target share, 0.03 WOPR, 3.7ppg over 11 games with zero broken tackles. He's RB#2 but the Cowboys also carry Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah, so a Javonte injury wouldn't cleanly funnel work to him. Floor is bench-clutter; ceiling only appears with an injury ahead of a crowded depth chart. Waiver-wire profile.

emanuel wilson.verdict: Two straight full 17-game seasons at 5.6ppg make him a stable, snap-earning depth back with standalone flex weeks
emanuel wilson.report: High-durability, modest-volume back: 125 carries and 15 catches in 2025, 31% snaps, 7 broken tackles. Efficiency slipped (4.0 ypc, -0.45 rush EPA/g) so the volume itself is the value, not the per-touch work. Ceiling is RB3 flex value if he climbs the committee; floor is a low-usage rotation piece behind a crowded room. Reliable availability is his edge.

will shipley.verdict: Pure Saquon insurance; 12% snaps and 1.0ppg mean nothing until Barkley misses time
will shipley.report: Bottom quadrant: 2.9% target share, 0.04 WOPR, negative rush and rec EPA, zero broken tackles on tiny volume. As RB behind an elite workhorse he has no standalone value, and Tank Bigsby now sits ahead in the pecking order clouding the handcuff path. The entire case is a Barkley injury, which would deliver a league-winning workload — a genuine but binary bet.

devin singletary.verdict: Proven 6.4ppg receiving back but now buried behind Skattebo and Tracy on the Giants depth chart
devin singletary.report: Solid volume history: 119 carries, 18 catches, 6.4ppg, positive rec EPA/g and 31 first downs in 2025 — a passing-down contributor. But 3.7 ypc and 1.8 yards before contact show the efficiency is fading at age/mileage, and the Giants clearly prefer Skattebo and Tracy going forward. Floor is a change-of-pace veteran; ceiling requires injuries above him.

tyler badie.verdict: Denver's designated third-down back with a strong 1.31 pts/touch, but volume is capped as RB4
tyler badie.report: Low-volume, receiving-tilted profile: 31 targets to just 8 carries, 5.3% target share, 1.31 points per touch. The efficiency per touch is real but the role is narrow with Dobbins, Harvey and Coleman ahead. Ceiling is PPR-only flex spike weeks if the passing-down role expands; floor is a specialist who rarely clears single digits. Depth chart is the ceiling-killer.

tahj brooks.verdict: Third on the Bengals chart with 5% snaps and negative EPA; nothing here to draft
tahj brooks.report: Bottom-quadrant fade: 0.5% target share, 0.01 WOPR, -0.34 rush EPA/g, one first down over 12 games. Chase Brown is entrenched and Perine is the veteran backup, leaving Brooks with no realistic path to touches barring multiple injuries. No efficiency signal to bet on either. Pure end-of-bench dart with a very low ceiling.

trevor etienne.verdict: Buried fourth in Carolina behind Hubbard; 6% snaps and no receiving role limit any upside
trevor etienne.report: Low volume across the board: 0.6% target share, 20 carries, 4.7 ypc but only 7 first downs. The 2.4 yards before contact hint at some burst, yet with Hubbard, Brooks and Dillon ahead there's no path to volume. Ceiling is a handful of spike weeks if injuries clear the room; floor is inactive most weeks. Speculative only.

seth mcgowan.verdict: Undrafted-type rookie behind Jonathan Taylor and Giddens; no NFL usage to project
seth mcgowan.report: No data to work with — a rookie RB#3 stuck behind an elite workhorse in Jonathan Taylor and second-year Giddens. Opportunity is essentially zero without a JT injury, and even then Giddens is next in line. Ceiling is a deep-injury dart; floor is a practice-squad-adjacent body. Nothing in the given profile supports a pick.

kendre miller.verdict: Talented but perpetually hurt; 7 broken tackles on 47 carries flashes ability the injuries keep erasing
kendre miller.report: Efficiency flash on tiny volume: 4.1 ypc, 2.6 yards after contact, 7 broken tackles in just 7 games — the low-volume/good-efficiency quadrant that needs opportunity. Problem is a Questionable tag continuing a chronic injury pattern and a depth chart with Etienne and Kamara ahead. Ceiling is real if healthy and given a role; floor is another lost season on IR.

jawhar jordan.verdict: Tiny sample but elite tackle-breaking (8 in 4 games) makes him a real dart if Houston's room thins
jawhar jordan.report: Low-volume, high-efficiency breakout profile: 7.4ppg, 4.5 ypc, 2.4 before/2.1 after contact and 8 broken tackles in only 4 games, plus a 30% snap share when active. He sits behind Montgomery and Woody Marks, so volume isn't guaranteed. Sleeper: the per-touch explosiveness clearly outruns his last-round ADP — start taking him in the final rounds as an upside stash if either back ahead slips.

kaleb johnson.verdict: Rookie with a brutal -0.77 rush EPA/g and 9% snaps; efficiency red flags outweigh the pedigree
kaleb johnson.report: Bottom-quadrant warning: aDOT -4.0, 0.00 WOPR, 1.3 yards before contact and -0.77 rush EPA/g over 10 games — poor efficiency on the little he saw. He's now RB#4 behind Dowdle and Warren, so volume is unlikely too. The data contradicts any buy-low case; ceiling needs both a role change and an efficiency rebound. Fade until usage shifts.

kene nwangwu.verdict: Kick-return specialist, not an offensive back; 4% snaps and -6.0 aDOT say no fantasy path
kene nwangwu.report: Special-teams profile: 0.5% target share, 4% snap share, two first downs over 12 games. He offers return value, not scrimmage touches, and sits fifth behind Hall, Allen and Davis. There is no volume or efficiency signal supporting offensive production. Floor and ceiling are both near replacement level in fantasy terms.

isaac guerendo.verdict: Explosive 2024 tape (5.0 ypc, 0.95 pts/touch) but PUP and stuck behind CMC caps 2026
isaac guerendo.report: His 2024 was legitimately strong — 84 carries at 5.0 ypc, 9.5 yards per target, 0.95 points per touch, the efficient/low-volume quadrant. But a PUP designation wipes out early availability and he's buried behind McCaffrey with James also ahead. Ceiling is a genuine CMC-injury lottery ticket given the talent; floor is a lost year if the health issue lingers.

brashard smith.verdict: Camp reports have him as KC's surprise No. 2 with Reid praising his receiving — a live sleeper
brashard smith.report: Rookie already flashing a pass-catching role: 35 targets, 25 catches, 6.6% target share and 0.92 points per touch in 2025, the receiving-back skill set. The fresh camp note that he's running No. 2 ahead of Demercado with Reid praising his routes is the freshest signal and raises the floor. Sleeper: a passing-down role in Mahomes' offense clearly beats his last-round ADP — take him in the final two rounds.

bam knight.verdict: Quietly usable dual-threat: 5.5ppg, 0.10 WOPR and 31 first downs, but poor rush EPA caps upside
bam knight.report: Decent volume for the tier: 82 carries, 22 catches, 6.3% target share, 0.10 WOPR and 31 first downs across 12 games — receiving work gives PPR floor. The -1.37 rush EPA/g and 3.3 ypc are ugly, so the volume is more empty than efficient. Ceiling is spot-start flex value if the role holds; floor is a low-end committee body. Missing depth data adds uncertainty.

dylan laube.verdict: Behind Jeanty with 3% snaps and 0.4 yards before contact; no usage case to make
dylan laube.report: Bottom-quadrant profile: 0.8% target share, 0.01 WOPR, 3% snaps and a dismal 0.4 yards before contact per rush over 17 games. With Ashton Jeanty locked in as the workhorse, there's no volume runway. Neither the opportunity nor the efficiency data support a pick. Deep-league handcuff at best.

rasheen ali.verdict: Third-down flier behind Henry and Justice Hill; 3.0 before but 0.4 after contact is a red flag
rasheen ali.report: Tiny receiving sample: 3.7% target share, 1.51 points per touch but only 3 first downs and a bizarre 0.4 yards after contact on 15 games. Derrick Henry dominates carries and Justice Hill owns passing downs, leaving Ali no clear role. Ceiling is emergency flex if two backs fall; floor is inactive. Not enough signal to draft outside deep dynasty.

jacob saylors.verdict: Fourth-string Lion with 1% snaps; roster filler with no projectable path to touches
jacob saylors.report: Effectively no data — 1% snap share, one first down over the season. Detroit's backfield runs through Gibbs with Pacheco added, burying Saylors on the depth chart. The 3.0 yards after contact on a handful of carries is noise, not signal. Both floor and ceiling sit at replacement level; undraftable in standard formats.

deejay dallas.verdict: Veteran sixth on the Jaguars chart; special-teams profile with no offensive volume
deejay dallas.report: Career profile is a return man and emergency back: 6% snaps, one first down, 0.5% target share. Six deep on the depth chart behind Tuten and a young room, there's no realistic touch share. Prior 5.4 ypc on nine carries is a meaningless sample. Nothing here supports a draft pick in any redraft format.

josh williams.verdict: Fourth on the Bucs chart with a 2-game sample and 0.0 yards after contact; not draftable
josh williams.report: No usable data: 4% snaps over 3 games, zero first downs, -0.93 rush EPA/g. Bucky Irving is entrenched with Gainwell and Tucker ahead, so Williams has no path to volume. The tiny sample shows no efficiency to dream on either. Pure roster filler; floor and ceiling are both near zero for fantasy purposes.

kyle juszczyk.verdict: Veteran FB with pure receiving role — low-volume, low-ceiling, undraftable in redraft PPR
kyle juszczyk.report: Low-volume, decent-efficiency quadrant: 5.5% target share and 0.10 WOPR mean he's a checkdown/blocking specialist, not a fantasy asset. His 2.04 pts/tgt and 46% snap share are stable but produce only ~3.4 PPG, which is roster-clogging in a 12-team league. Rushing is negligible (-1.5 ypc, -1.5 before contact). No path to volume at RB4 and age 34. Fine real-life player, zero draft value.

hunter luepke.verdict: Dallas FB/hybrid with tiny snap share — depth flier only, no standalone value
hunter luepke.report: Low-volume, modest-efficiency profile: 3.3% target share, 21% snaps, and only 16 carries. His 4.4 ypc with 2.8 yards after contact shows he can run when asked, but the opportunity simply isn't there behind Dallas's backfield. At RB6 on the depth chart, only a cascade of injuries opens a role. PPG (2.2) is too low to matter in redraft.

alec ingold.verdict: Blocking fullback whose usage dropped in 2025 — no fantasy relevance
alec ingold.report: Deep low-volume, poor-efficiency territory: production fell from 1.5 to 0.8 PPG as targets and carries dried up, with negative rec EPA/g. The 37% snap share is blocking-driven, not touch-driven, and he sits RB5. No trend supports a rebound. Purely a real-NFL role player; leave undrafted.

adam prentice.verdict: Denver special-teamer/FB with negligible touches — undraftable
adam prentice.report: Bottom quadrant: 1.7% target share, 19% snaps, 0.03 WOPR — essentially no fantasy footprint. The 3.0 yards before contact on limited carries is a blocking-scheme artifact, not usable volume. RB6 with no clear injury-driven path to touches. Nothing here for redraft.

connor heyward.verdict: Hybrid TE/RB buried behind Bowers and Mayer — efficiency blip, no real opportunity
connor heyward.report: Ultra-low-volume with a misleading efficiency line: 0.61 rush EPA/g and 2.9 ypc on 15 carries is noise, and his 9% snap share and 0.9% target share confirm he's a rotational piece. Bowers dominates the Raiders passing game, capping any receiving path. Fun gadget usage but no volume to build a fantasy case. Waiver-wire at best.

michael burton.verdict: 33-year-old blocking FB with no 2025 data — pure depth body
michael burton.report: No 2025 usage and a 2024 line of 1.7 PPG on tiny volume place him firmly in the fade quadrant. The 2.93 pts/tgt in 2024 came on just 10 targets and won't scale; 1.1 ypc shows no rushing role. At RB4 with 11 years of experience, he's a blocking specialist, not a fantasy option. Skip entirely.

puka nacua.verdict: League-best per-route WR with 30% target share and elite efficiency — a true 1.1-caliber WR anchor.
puka nacua.report: High volume + elite efficiency quadrant: 30.1% target share, 0.69 WOPR, 2.26 pts/tgt and a league-leading targets-per-route mark. The 375-point 2025 (22.1 PPG) is built on real usage, not TD luck (rec EPA 7.23/g). Ceiling is overall WR1; floor is dragged only by injury history (missed a game) and Adams siphoning 100+ targets. Playoff slate (DAL, @SEA, @TB) is fine. Volume this dominant survives even offensive regression.

ja'marr chase.verdict: 32% target share and 94% snaps keep him elite; 2025 dip was Burrow health, not talent decline.
ja'marr chase.report: High volume, efficiency slipped in 2025 (1.70 pts/tgt vs 2.30 in 2024) largely with Burrow banged up — the 32.1% target share and 0.74 WOPR are untouchable. Ceiling returns to his 2024 403-point, 23.7-PPG range if Burrow is healthy; floor is his 314-point 2025 line, still WR1 volume. Higgins takes 100+ targets but Chase's role is scheme-proof. Playoff draw (@CAR, @IND, BAL) is favorable early. QB health is the only swing.

jaxon smith-njigba.verdict: 36.8% target share and 0.90 WOPR — elite volume with a near-perfect 2025; only OC change tempers it.
jaxon smith-njigba.report: Peak volume + strong efficiency: 36.8% target share (highest since 2012), 0.90 WOPR, 2.21 pts/tgt and the lowest weekly variance (7.3) of any top WR. That consistency raises the floor meaningfully. Ceiling is overall WR1; the risk is Kubiak's departure — prior OC exits preceded explosive-play declines — plus added competition from Shaheed/Horton. Playoff @PHI/LAR/@CAR is mixed. Dominant target monopoly with a real safety net.

amon-ra st. brown.verdict: Three straight top-5 finishes and 31.7% target share make him the safest WR outside the top four.
amon-ra st. brown.report: High volume, reliable efficiency: 31.7% target share, 0.75 WOPR, back-to-back 315+ point seasons. Second-half surge (16.1 PPG once Campbell called plays) shows the ceiling; the LaPorta-back split (10.9 PPG with him) and new TE-focused OC Petzing are the real floor risks. Detroit funnels volume to its top WR regardless. Playoff @MIN/NYG/@CHI is workable with dome games. Floor is elite-safe, ceiling capped just below the top tier.

ceedee lamb.verdict: 2025 was TD-regression bad luck on missed games; volume and QB argue a rebound to WR1 range.
ceedee lamb.report: High volume, poor 2025 efficiency — but 1.72 pts/tgt with heavy red-zone work screams TD variance, not decline. He played only 13 games and still carried a 25.1% target share and 12.0 aDOT. Ceiling is his 2024 263-point form or better; floor is a repeat low-end WR1 line if Pickens keeps eating target share (down from 152 to 117 targets). Playoff @LAR/JAX/NYG with a Week 14 bye. You're buying the floor-plus-rebound, not the peak ceiling.

justin jefferson.verdict: Elite target share but a -0.81 rec EPA/g and unsettled QB room make this a rare risk at his price.
justin jefferson.report: Classic high-volume/poor-efficiency warning: 30.7% target share and 0.74 WOPR, but rec EPA cratered to -0.81/g and PPG fell to 11.9 on brutal QB play. Camp intel has Murray taking first-team reps and targeting Jefferson aggressively — a genuine upgrade signal if he wins the job. Ceiling is a full return to his 2024 317-point self; floor is another QB-suppressed year. Playoff DET/WSH/@NYJ is fine. Talent is elite; the offense around him is the question.

drake london.verdict: 33% target share with Penix healthy is WR1 volume; the whole case rides on the QB staying upright.
drake london.report: High volume, solid efficiency in a small sample: 29.7% target share, 0.73 WOPR, 91% snaps across only 12 games. Every Penix passing TD has gone to London and Mooney's exit didn't dent his usage. Ceiling is top-5 WR if Penix plays a full year; floor is ugly (11.9 PPG, high 12.0 stdev) if Penix's PCL issue recurs. Playoff @WSH/TB/NO is favorable. You're paying WR14 for a boom/bust dependent entirely on one QB's health.

rashee rice.verdict: 29% target share and elite red-zone role in KC, but knee ramp and Nagy's exit cloud the volume.
rashee rice.report: High volume in his 8 healthy games (29% target share, 0.53 WOPR held down by a 4.3 aDOT screen-heavy role). Camp reports him as KC's No. 1 but fatiguing post-knee-surgery, so a gradual ramp is likely — Week 1 usage won't be full. Ceiling is top-12 if the Reid offense feeds him like 2025; floor is depressed by the ramp and Nagy (who schemed for him) leaving. Playoff NE/SF/@LAC is average. Talent-plus-role, but health and scheme are live risks.

nico collins.verdict: Clear alpha with 12.7 aDOT and strong per-target efficiency — a high floor if the health and O-line hold.
nico collins.report: Efficient volume: 24.2% target share, 12.7 aDOT, 3.10 pts/touch and a WR2-overall pace in his 2024 healthy games. The knock is a genuinely bad Texans O-line and repeated concussion/injury absences (15 games in 2025). Ceiling is a top-8 WR season; floor is a missed-time, QB-suppressed line (his number actually dipped in Stroud's healthy games). Playoff JAX/@PHI/@GB is mixed. A boring, high-floor pick for someone punting early RB — talent is real.

garrett wilson.verdict: 0.92 WOPR and 35% target share when healthy; talent is WR1-caliber, the offense and QB are not.
garrett wilson.report: Elite volume in a tiny 7-game sample (35.4% target share, 56.3% air-yards share, 0.92 WOPR) before injury ended his year. Talent alone can produce WR1 numbers — 5 of 6 WR1 finishes in 2024 before he got hurt. Ceiling is a 140-target, top-12 season; floor is Jets-offense dysfunction with Geno (a downgrade from Rodgers) and rookie Adonai Mitchell nibbling targets. Playoff @ARI/NE/MIN is decent. Massive target hog trapped in a shaky offense.

a.j. brown.verdict: Clear-cut No. 1 in New England with a deep-ball QB fit; big ceiling, low floor on knee/hamstring risk.
a.j. brown.report: Efficient downfield volume: 28.7% target share, 11.8 aDOT, 91% snaps, and beat coverage names him NE's undisputed alpha post-trade with Doubs the clear No. 2. Ceiling is top-5 numbers if Maye's deep accuracy connects with him (his second-half-healthy 2025 form). Floor is real — two hamstrings plus two cleaned-up knees at 29 make missed time likely. Playoff @KC/@NYJ/DEN is average. High variance: same boom/bust shape as London for different reasons.

chris olave.verdict: 29% target share and a WR7 finish when healthy; extension signed, clot cleared — buy the volume, fear the head.
chris olave.report: Rebounded to 268 points (15.8 PPG) on a 29.2% target share and 11.8 aDOT, notably better once Shough took over at QB. Extension signed Aug 5 and blood-thinner restrictions lifted removes off-field noise. Ceiling is a repeat WR1 line if Shough sustains the deep-shot volume; floor is his scary concussion history plus Jordan Tyson eating into his post-Shaheed target bump. Playoff @TB/ARI/@ATL is fine. High-usage bounce-back with a real medical asterisk.

george pickens.verdict: 17.2 PPG and 2.13 pts/tgt even as Dallas's WR2 — a WR1-upside profile priced as a WR3.
george pickens.report: Efficient on modest volume: 22.5% target share but 5.22 rec EPA/g, 10.4 yds/tgt and a 292-point, 17.2-PPG 2025 while sharing with Lamb. He was a top-8 WR even with Lamb active and the overall WR1 the month Lamb was out. Ceiling climbs as Dak chemistry (slow to start last year) is now established; floor is limited given full 17-game durability. Playoff @LAR/JAX/NYG, Week 14 bye. Strong value — a de facto Lamb handcuff with standalone WR1 spikes.

malik nabers.verdict: Rookie WR6 on top-of-NFL target volume, but knee recovery and a run-leaning Harbaugh offense cap it.
malik nabers.report: Elite talent on a tiny 2025 sample (4 games, knee) after a 274-point rookie year at NFL-leading target volume (27.1% share, 15.9 aDOT). Camp says he 'feels great' but as of Aug 5 he's still limited in team drills — monitor. Ceiling is a top-6 return if fully healthy; floor is lower on the knee plus Harbaugh/Nagy pushing Nagy's run-heavy scheme and a weak Giants passing game. Playoff CLE/@DET/@DAL. Boom talent, but health and offensive environment both trend down.

tetairoa mcmillan.verdict: 87% snaps and 45.9% air-yards share as a rookie; a clean Year-2 breakout if Bryce Young keeps climbing.
tetairoa mcmillan.report: Volume already alpha-level for a rookie: 25.7% target share, 45.9% air-yards share, 122 targets on 87% snaps, low 6.9 stdev. Efficiency (1.73 pts/tgt) reflects typical rookie miscues that should shrink. Ceiling is a WR15-20 season if Young's positive trend holds; floor is capped by a still-shaky Carolina offense. Playoff CIN/@PIT/SEA is average. The swing factor is the QB — but the target monopoly is locked in and points forward to growth.

zay flowers.verdict: WR12 in Lamar's 13 games with 30% target share; new pass-friendly OC could unlock a career year.
zay flowers.report: Efficient volume: 29.9% target share, 2.06 pts/tgt, 10.3 yds/tgt and a WR12 pace in the games Lamar played. New OC Doyle projects a league-average pass rate — a big jump for a chronically run-heavy offense — and Andrews' efficiency collapse opens targets. Ceiling is 18+ PPG if Baltimore lifts its pass volume; floor is another run-suppressed slate with Bateman as WR2. Playoff @PIT/CLE/@CIN. Fresh $140M deal cements his role. Upside tied to the offense speeding up.

devonta smith.verdict: Now Philly's undisputed No. 1 post-Brown trade; target share should jump toward 30% in a better scheme fit.
devonta smith.report: Efficient on a suppressed 24.6% target share while behind Brown, with prior stretches showing his targets/route spike near 30% when Brown sits. The trade makes him the every-down alpha, and new OC Mannion's outside-heavy scheme fits him better than last year's slot miscasting. Ceiling is a top-5 breakout; floor is a repeat ~12 PPG if Hurts' rushing caps pass volume. Minor camp hamstring, no long-term concern. Playoff SEA/HOU/@SF. Clear opportunity opening ahead of him.

emeka egbuka.verdict: 20.5 PPG through five weeks as a rookie; now the clear No. 1 with Evans gone — big Year-2 upside.
emeka egbuka.report: Elite rookie start (20.5 PPG through 5) on a 23.6% target share before a hamstring tanked his snaps (85% to 50% as Evans/McMillan returned). Still 11.5 PPG counting the down weeks. Ceiling is a genuine WR1 if he's the healthy alpha with Evans gone; floor is dampened by new OC Zac Robinson (a scheme downgrade risk) and Godwin/McMillan splitting work. Currently listed Questionable — monitor the hamstring. Playoff NO/@ATL/LAR. Real breakout profile at a fair price.

davante adams.verdict: WR9 on TD volume, not efficiency (-106 yards-over-expected); regression looms behind Nacua.
davante adams.report: High volume, poor true efficiency: 25.1% target share but only 6.9 yds/tgt and a -106 yards-over-expected — his 2025 WR9 finish leaned on 14 TDs that likely regress toward 12. The Rams' pace and McVay scheme keep him relevant, but he's clearly WR2 behind Nacua's 30% share. Ceiling is another red-zone-fueled WR2 line; floor sags on age, hamstring history and TD regression. Playoff DAL/@SEA/@TB. Fine but capped — better ceiling bets exist in this range.

ladd mcconkey.verdict: Year-3 breakout hopes hinge on a target share he doesn't yet own; 21% share and 0.50 WOPR are modest.
ladd mcconkey.report: Efficiency dipped in 2025 (1.71 pts/tgt vs 2.15) as his target share fell to 21.1% with a soft 0.50 WOPR — more low-end WR2 than breakout so far. The bull case is a Herbert/McDaniel offense funneling him 10+ targets, but Johnston likely holds a real share (a 25/22 split is plausible). Ceiling is a WR1 leap if he commands 28%+ of targets; floor is another 10-11 PPG year. Playoff SF/@MIA/KC. Talented, but the volume he needs isn't yet secured.

terry mclaurin.verdict: Elite in-game usage but 2025 efficiency crashed; Diggs caps ceiling — a volume bet on a Daniels rebound.
terry mclaurin.report: 2024 breakout (15.8 ppg, 2.29 pts/tgt) collapsed to 6.7 ppg in 2025 as TDs regressed and he missed time, though he kept elite in-game usage (23.2% share, 0.61 WOPR, 14.0 aDOT). Diggs' arrival trims target share but he stays the clear WR1 with Daniels. Ceiling is a bounce toward 2024 if the offense recovers; floor is a 2025 repeat on a shaky O-line at age 31.

tee higgins.verdict: Efficient, high-floor WR2 with WR1 upside whenever Burrow's healthy — injury risk is the only real knock.
tee higgins.report: Steady line: 12.4 ppg in 2025, 13.1 in 2024, efficient at 2.16 pts/tgt behind Chase (18.3% share, 0.50 WOPR). Ceiling is top-8 when Burrow's healthy and the offense rolls; floor is tied to his own and Burrow's injury history (15 games in 2025). Only real competition is Chase ahead of him. Playoffs @CAR/@IND/BAL are manageable.

jaylen waddle.verdict: New Denver WR1 role plus league-leading pass volume make this a strong ascending bet at a WR20s price.
jaylen waddle.report: Owned a strong Miami profile even in a run-heavy scheme (23.3% share, 0.65 WOPR, 42.7% air-yards). Now Denver's clear WR1 on a team that led the NFL in pass attempts behind a top-graded O-line and Bo Nix. Ceiling is a career year as a true alpha; floor is target dispersion with Sutton and a Questionable tag, though he's historically durable (7 games missed in 5 years).

jameson williams.verdict: Big-play, TD-reliant WR3 whose ceiling needs a St. Brown absence; volume caps the floor.
jameson williams.report: Back-to-back ~12.5 ppg seasons on big-play efficiency (11.0 yds/tgt) but modest volume (18.6% share, 0.50 WOPR) behind St. Brown; production spikes when St. Brown or LaPorta sit. A new OC may funnel more to LaPorta, compressing his share. Boom/bust: 8 sub-10-yard games in 3 years but home-run-speed upside. Playoffs @MIN/NYG/@CHI mixed.

carnell tate.verdict: Pro-ready rookie with a WR1 path in Tennessee, but zero data — a bet on talent and target vacancy.
carnell tate.report: No NFL data; rookie stepping in as Tennessee's LWR1, with Cam Ward's downfield, contested-catch style suiting his game and scouts calling him the most pro-ready of the class. Ceiling is an immediate every-week starter if he wins the alpha role over Ridley and Wan'Dale; floor is a slow rookie ramp on a rebuilding offense. Playoffs IND/@LV/PIT manageable. Pure projection at this price.

rome odunze.verdict: Pre-injury WR1 usage plus vacated Moore targets in a Ben Johnson offense — a clean Year-3 breakout bet.
rome odunze.report: Before a foot injury he was a WR1 (16.1 ppg, 23.6% share, 0.60 WOPR); the full 2025 line looks tame (8.6 ppg) but the modest 1.62 pts/tgt was volume-driven, not TD luck. DJ Moore's exit frees red-zone work, and Year 3 with Caleb Williams in a Ben Johnson offense points up. Burden and Loveland split targets. Playoffs @BUF/GB/DET are tough.

luther burden iii.verdict: Efficient rookie slot with a real target vacancy, but Odunze/Loveland crowd the path — upside dart.
luther burden iii.report: Rookie slot line was efficient (2.13 pts/tgt, 10.9 yds/tgt) on tiny volume (13.1% share, 0.27 WOPR, 7.7 aDOT); low volume plus strong efficiency is the breakout quadrant if the ~150 vacated targets open up. But Odunze and Loveland both project 100+ targets, so the path is contested. Ben Johnson is reportedly high on him. Unproven, with Worthy-style bust risk.

dj moore.verdict: Bounce-back bet on a Buffalo opening and Josh Allen after a dismal, low-efficiency 2025.
dj moore.report: 2024 in Chicago was a WR1 season (14.0 ppg, 140 tgt); 2025 cratered to 10.0 ppg with a 16.1% share and weak 0.80 rec EPA/g as he fell to the 4th option. Now in Buffalo inheriting Diggs' vacated role with Josh Allen — a pure opportunity bet against poor 2025 tape. Shakir, Palmer and Coleman still compete. Playoffs CHI/@DEN/@MIA okay.

courtland sutton.verdict: Proven volume but Waddle now siphons the target and red-zone share — ceiling capped, floor solid.
courtland sutton.report: Two straight ~13-14 ppg seasons on strong volume (21.1% share, 0.56 WOPR, 52 first downs) but only average efficiency (1.77 pts/tgt). Waddle's arrival and Sutton's own public concession of the 1A role should trim his target and red-zone work, capping ceiling absent a Waddle injury. A high-volume, modest-efficiency profile now at real risk. Playoffs @LV/BUF/@NE.

michael pittman jr..verdict: PPR-friendly target volume, but a WR2 move to Pittsburgh behind Metcalf threatens the one thing that fed him.
michael pittman jr..report: Reliable target earner (111 tgt each of the last two years, 86% snaps) but poor efficiency (1.82 pts/tgt, 7.1 yds/tgt) — a high-volume, low-efficiency chain-mover. Moving to Pittsburgh as the clear WR2 behind Metcalf likely cuts the volume that carried him. Rodgers' short game fits, but his PPR value hinges on a target count that may shrink. Playoffs BAL/CAR/@TEN.

alec pierce.verdict: Hyper-efficient deep threat, but a PUP tag and boom/bust deep role make him a volatile flex.
alec pierce.report: Elite big-play profile: 19.0 aDOT, 40.6% air-yards share, 3.72 rec EPA/g and 2.18 pts/tgt — efficiency that far outruns his 17.6% target share. But he opens on PUP, a real availability flag, and the deep role is boom/bust (8.5 weekly stdev). If healthy and Colts QB play holds, spike weeks come; floor is a missed ramp and quiet stretches.

marvin harrison jr..verdict: Red-zone role and talent give TD-driven breakout upside, but efficiency and McBride/Wilson competition cap the floor.
marvin harrison jr..report: Down Year 2 (7.5 ppg, 12 g, 71% snaps) but real usage: 18.1% share, 0.50 WOPR and #2 in the NFL in end-zone targets — a genuine red-zone role. Efficiency (1.75 pts/tgt) still lags, McBride is the clear #1, and Wilson competes. Ceiling is a TD-fueled Year-3 breakout in a pass-heavy offense; floor is another inefficient, QB-dependent year. Playoffs NYJ/@NO/LV soft.

dk metcalf.verdict: Volume keeps him a WR3, but a shrunken deep role and aging QB cap any real ceiling.
dk metcalf.report: Steady ~11 ppg both years on solid volume (22.4% share, 0.60 WOPR), but his aDOT fell to 10.5 in a Steelers scheme that rarely throws deep, cutting the vertical role that defines him. Rodgers' age and Pittman competing for looks limit upside. A high-volume, middling-efficiency WR3 profile. Playoffs BAL/CAR/@TEN mixed.

jordyn tyson.verdict: Talented rookie behind Olave, but a weak Saints offense and no data make him pure speculation.
jordyn tyson.report: No NFL data; first-round rookie ramping alongside Olave with a red-zone camp TD noted. Ceiling is a quick complementary role if his hamstring stays clear and Olave draws coverage; floor is a slow rookie start on a low-scoring Saints offense with shaky QB play. Playoffs @TB/ARI/@ATL. Speculative at this price.

mike evans.verdict: Elite usage when upright, but age, soft-tissue injuries and a crowded new SF room make him high-variance.
mike evans.report: When healthy in 2025 he owned a 24.3% share and 0.61 WOPR, but he played just 8 games and fell to 5.0 ppg amid soft-tissue issues; 2024 was a 14.1 ppg WR1. Now 32-33 on a new team in SF with a fresh quad strain and Deebo/Pearsall/Kirk competition. A classic TD-reliant profile carrying serious age and injury risk. Playoffs @LAC/@KC/PHI tough.

parker washington.verdict: Sleeper: elite late-season yards/route in the slot at a Round-9 price with a clear efficiency edge.
parker washington.report: Broke out late in 2025: 10.9 ppg, 18% share, and 2nd in the NFL in yards/route over the final 8 games (behind only Nacua). His slot role helps him dodge tough boundary corners early. Competition from BTJ, Meyers and Hunter is real, but the finishing form and camp buzz support the price. Low-ish volume, strong efficiency — start taking him in Round 9.

christian watson.verdict: Elite big-play efficiency but a GB committee caps volume — high-variance breakout dart.
christian watson.report: Elite per-target efficiency (2.41 pts/tgt, 11.1 yds/tgt, 17.8 aDOT, 0.55 WOPR) but volume has never been consistent — he's never topped 7 tgt/game even at his best. He projects as Green Bay's #1, yet Reed and Golden keep it a committee. A low-volume, high-efficiency deep threat with breakout upside if targets climb and a boom/bust floor. Playoffs MIA/@CHI/HOU okay.

matthew golden.verdict: ESPN sleeper call, but weak rookie volume and efficiency in a crowded GB room don't support it yet.
matthew golden.report: Rookie line was quiet across the board: 4.1 ppg, 12.4% share, 0.32 WOPR, 1.59 pts/tgt — low volume and low efficiency, the fade quadrant. ESPN's early-opportunity sleeper call isn't supported by the usage; Watson and Reed sit ahead in a spread-it-around GB offense, so I skip the badge. Needs a real leap to matter. Ceiling is a mid-season role, floor is bench filler.

michael wilson.verdict: Sleeper: real 120+ target volume and late-2025 WR1 form at a Round-9 price the field ignores.
michael wilson.report: Quietly a high-volume producer in 2025: 126 targets, 19.2% share, 0.51 WOPR, 51 first downs, 81% snaps, and WR1 form down the stretch. Efficiency is average (1.75 pts/tgt) and MHJ competes, but the target floor is real and the price is a discount. High variance (10.3 stdev). Start taking him in Round 9 as a volume value. Playoffs NYJ/@NO/LV soft.

brian thomas jr..verdict: Sleeper: a 24-year-old former alpha whose 2025 crash was injury-driven — Round-9 bounce-back upside.
brian thomas jr..report: 2024 was a 16.7 ppg alpha season (133 tgt, 2.14 pts/tgt); 2025 collapsed to 8.2 ppg playing hurt while usage stayed real (19.3% share, 0.51 WOPR). Only 24, on a pass-heavy offense — a strong bounce-back bet. A brutal early CB schedule and Washington/Meyers/Hunter competition are the risks. Ceiling is a return to WR1; start taking him in Round 9. Playoffs @HOU/@DAL/WSH.

denzel boston.verdict: Big-bodied rookie WR3 in a bad Browns passing game; staff-sleeper hype outruns the opportunity
denzel boston.report: No NFL data; a Day-2 rookie sitting WR3 behind Jeudy, Concepcion and Tillman in one of the league's worst QB situations. Ceiling case is contested-catch size winning red-zone looks and a Jeudy injury opening volume. Floor is near-zero snaps if the vets hold up. Camp catch clips and 'monster season' TikToks move price, not projection — I'm not badging sleeper because the depth chart and QB play cap the realistic ceiling. Rookie dart only.

adonai mitchell.verdict: High air-yards share but rec EPA -1.01 and 15% target share — volume-adjacent, poor efficiency, buried behind Wilson
adonai mitchell.report: Year-3 profile is a warning quadrant: 30% air-yards share and 14.9 aDOT show a downfield role, but 1.19 pts/tgt and -1.01 rec EPA/g mean he's not converting it. Only 15.3% target share and 51% snaps behind Garrett Wilson. Ceiling is a Geno-Smith deep connection clicking; floor is the same empty 4.9 PPG. ESPN's 'developing opportunity' call is fair on talent, but the efficiency data contradicts a breakout, so no sleeper badge.

de'zhaun stribling.verdict: Rookie whose path just opened — Pearsall's season-ending surgery clears a real WR3 role in Shanahan's YAC scheme
de'zhaun stribling.report: No pro data, but the depth chart shifted: with Pearsall out for the year (Aug 5 surgery), a rookie behind aging Evans and Deebo has a genuine target lane in a YAC-friendly offense. Ceiling is a mid-season role as the field-stretching complement; floor is inactive weeks and a questionable tag now. The 21k-like TikTok tells you ADP is about to climb. Start taking him in the last two rounds as a lottery ticket on the opened opportunity.

germie bernard.verdict: Rookie slot WR3 behind Metcalf and Pittman — no clear target path in Pittsburgh
germie bernard.report: No NFL data and a crowded room: DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman own the volume, leaving a rookie slot man with scraps. Ceiling requires an injury ahead of him and Rodgers-era-style volume that isn't there. Floor is a healthy scratch most weeks. Chatter is generic hype with no camp specifics, so it's pure price noise. Deep bench flier only.

antonio williams.verdict: Rookie slot flier whose 'wide-open depth chart' thesis just got crowded by the Diggs signing
antonio williams.report: Multiple analysts flagged an immediate slot role, but that call predates Washington adding Stefon Diggs, who slots into the exact SWR role — so the wide-open-depth-chart premise is now stale. Behind McLaurin, Diggs and Dyami Brown, the target math got worse, not better. Ceiling is a savvy route-runner earning Daniels' trust if injuries hit; floor is a rookie inactive. I'm skipping the sleeper badge specifically because the Diggs move undercuts the opening.

tre tucker.verdict: Locked-in WR1 role — 95% snaps, 19% target share, positive rec EPA — badly underpriced at this ADP
tre tucker.report: Two straight years of growth (129→162 pts) with a strong quadrant: 19% target share, 0.47 WOPR, 95% snap share and +1.28 rec EPA/g — real volume AND efficiency, not TD luck. As the Raiders' clear alpha with thin competition (Nailor, Bech), his floor is a weekly flex and his ceiling is low-end WR2. An ADP near 168 for a locked-in 95%-snap target earner is a value; start taking him around round 12-13 as a sleeper who beats his cost.

jalen nailor.verdict: Efficient on tiny volume (1.90 pts/tgt) but WOPR 0.29 behind Tucker caps the ceiling
jalen nailor.report: Classic low-volume, good-efficiency profile: 8.4 yds/tgt and 6.0 YAC/rush look nice, but 11.7% target share and 0.29 WOPR are the story — he's the No. 2 behind Tucker with no clear path to volume. Ceiling is spike weeks on deep shots; floor is 5-6 PPG. FantasyPros listed him as a deep sleeper, but the blocked volume behind Tucker keeps the realistic ceiling below his ADP, so no badge. Streamer at best.

omar cooper jr..verdict: Undrafted-caliber rookie with no depth-chart footing on the Jets — pure dynasty-name flier
omar cooper jr..report: No NFL data and no Sleeper depth-chart match, which itself signals a fringe camp body behind Garrett Wilson and Mitchell. Ceiling is a practice-squad-to-active surprise; floor is not making the 53. The only chatter is dynasty-value speculation, which is price/perception, not opportunity. Ignore in redraft.

rashod bateman.verdict: 2024's 175 points was TD-fueled; 2025 collapse to 55 exposes the low target share behind Flowers
