rashod bateman.report: The two seasons tell the story: 10.3 PPG in 2024 on 2.43 pts/tgt (unsustainable TD rate) crashed to 3.3 PPG in 2025 with -0.13 rec EPA/g and just 11.9% target share. Zay Flowers is the clear alpha and the role is a low-volume perimeter one. Ceiling needs the TDs to return; floor is what we just saw. This is a TD-dependent decline profile, not a bounce-back buy.

jauan jennings.verdict: Proven 19.9% target earner but a move to Minnesota buries him behind Jefferson and Addison
jauan jennings.report: In San Francisco he posted real volume — 19.9% target share, 0.48 WOPR, 173 pts — a legit high-usage profile. But on his new team he's the SWR3 behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, a sharp downgrade in opportunity. Ceiling is WR3 value if Addison misses time; floor is a low-target afterthought in a top-heavy target tree. The talent is there; the Minnesota role math is the problem.

tank dell.verdict: Returning from a devastating knee injury; talented when healthy but a stash, not a volume bet
tank dell.report: 2024 showed a usable WR (140 pts, 8.2 PPG, 1.73 pts/tgt) before multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap wiped 2025. He just returned to limited practice Aug 5 with coaches saying he's 'not being rushed' — a clear signal this is a late-season upside play, not Week 1 volume. Behind Collins, Higgins and Noel. Ceiling is a healthy stretch run; floor is missed time again. Injury-history dart.

zachariah branch.verdict: Rookie gadget/return man behind Drake London — limited passing-game volume in Atlanta
zachariah branch.report: No NFL data; a rookie slotting as SWR2 in a run-leaning Falcons offense where Drake London dominates targets. Ceiling is manufactured touches and return value adding sneaky PPR points; floor is a low-snap specialist. Camp 'making plays' clips are encouraging but non-specific on volume. Deep bench flier in the final rounds.

ricky pearsall.verdict: Season-ending PCL surgery confirmed Aug 5 — undraftable, remove entirely
ricky pearsall.report: A verifiable fact overrides everything else: Pearsall underwent season-ending PCL surgery on Aug 5. His 2025 flashes (2.97 rec EPA/g, 0.49 WOPR in nine games) were genuinely promising, which makes it a shame, but there is no 2026 to project. Proj is 0. Do not draft him in redraft.

darnell mooney.verdict: 2024's 193-point deep threat cratered to 82; new team, weak QB and Nabers ahead all cut against him
darnell mooney.report: The split is stark: 11.4 PPG in 2024 fell to 4.8 in 2025 as the deep-ball hits dried up (aDOT 14.2 but only 1.14 pts/tgt). Now the RWR2 behind Malik Nabers in a struggling Giants offense with unsettled QB play per camp reports. Ceiling is boom weeks on his vertical role if the offense functions; floor is the empty 2025 line repeating. Volume-adjacent but efficiency and situation say fade.

stefon diggs.verdict: Coming off a 210-point, 21.9% target-share, +4.14 rec-EPA season — badly underpriced despite age and a new team
stefon diggs.report: His 2025 was elite: 12.4 PPG, 21.9% target share, 0.47 WOPR and a standout +4.14 rec EPA/g on just 54% snaps — high volume with excellent efficiency at age 33. He signed with Washington (Aug 5) pairing with McLaurin, not replacing him, so target competition is real but he remains a proven separator. Note the playoff/bye data listed is stale from his FA status. Age is the risk; the production says start taking him well before his ADP as a sleeper.

tre' harris.verdict: Consistent but tiny-volume rookie season (0.24 WOPR) stuck as Chargers' third WR
tre' harris.report: Rookie line was low-variance and low-ceiling: 4.1 PPG, 2.9 stdev, 0.24 WOPR — he barely moved the target needle behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston. Ceiling requires an injury ahead of him and a bigger route share; floor is the quiet role we saw. Low volume with only okay efficiency keeps him a bench name. Wait-and-see.

ryan flournoy.verdict: Genuine efficiency edge (2.04 pts/tgt, 1.91 rec EPA, strong FD/route) on tiny volume behind Lamb and Pickens
ryan flournoy.report: The breakout-quadrant flag is real: on just 11.1% target share and 45% snaps he produced 2.04 pts/tgt, +1.91 rec EPA/g and elite first-downs-per-route — a strong per-opportunity edge. The catch is volume: he's SWR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, so the ceiling needs an injury to unlock it. Staff-named as a sleeper and the efficiency backs it — a final-round dart worth stashing if you value the profile, with the volume caveat stated.

jaylin noel.verdict: 6% target share, 26% snaps and now on PUP — no volume and a health flag in a crowded Houston room
jaylin noel.report: Rookie usage was minimal: 6% target share, 0.13 WOPR, 26% snaps, and he's currently on PUP. Efficiency (1.95 pts/tgt) was fine on the rare looks, but there's no volume behind Collins, Higgins and Dell. Ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead plus a clean bill of health; floor is inactive. The PUP designation is the freshest and most damning signal. Avoid in redraft.

xavier legette.verdict: Two years of poor efficiency (-0.27 rec EPA) and now losing his role to rookie McMillan
xavier legette.report: Volume-adjacent but the wrong kind: 14.3% target share with -0.27 rec EPA/g and 1.40 pts/tgt — he's not converting looks, and 2025 (89 pts) declined from 2024 (125). Rookie Tetairoa McMillan is now the alpha and Legette sits as low as RWR4 with a questionable tag. Ceiling needs efficiency he's never shown; floor is a marginalized role. High-volume-poor-efficiency profile whose volume is being taken away — fade.

jack bech.verdict: 8% target share as a rookie, third in a modest Raiders room — no path to fantasy volume yet
jack bech.report: Quiet rookie year: 2.5 PPG, 8% target share, 0.20 WOPR, 40% snaps — no meaningful volume or standout efficiency (1.46 pts/tgt). He sits behind Tucker and Nailor with limited target runway. Ceiling is a Year-2 leap if he climbs the depth chart; floor is the same afterthought role. Nothing in the usage argues for a redraft investment. Deep dynasty name only.

isaac teslaa.verdict: Efficient on tiny volume but buried behind ASB and Jamo — needs an injury to matter
isaac teslaa.report: Low-volume, good-efficiency quadrant: 5.7% target share and 0.17 WOPR but a healthy 2.81 pts/tgt and 13.0 aDOT show real downfield chops. The problem is the depth chart — Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams own this room, capping him as the WR3 at 40% snaps. Ceiling requires a vacancy ahead; floor is near-zero flex value. The 'need a chance' feature confirms the profile without a path.

chris bell.verdict: PUP rookie WR5 with no data — pure dynasty/dart-throw, not a redraft asset
chris bell.report: No NFL usage to interpret and currently on PUP, sitting fifth on Miami's depth behind Wease and Washington. There is no volume or efficiency signal to grade, so the projection is aspiration. Ceiling depends entirely on health and attrition in a thin but crowded-at-the-bottom room; floor is a redshirt. Leave him on waivers in redraft.

malik washington.verdict: Slot volume is opening in a gutted Miami room, but the 5.2 aDOT and negative EPA cap upside
malik washington.report: High-volume, poor-efficiency slot: 14.4% target share and 0.29 WOPR are real, yet a 5.2 aDOT and -0.58 rec EPA/g mean the yards and TDs don't follow the catches. With Miami's receiver room thinned out, his target share should climb, and PPR rewards the reception floor. Ceiling is a WR4/flex if volume spikes; floor is empty-calorie PPR points. Start taking him rounds 13-14 as the opportunity clearly widens.

jalen tolbert.verdict: 2024 flashed 8.9 ppg then cratered to 2.7 — new team, boom/bust dart in a thin room
jalen tolbert.report: Volume evaporated in 2025 (7.6% target share, 2.7 ppg) after a useful 2024 (79 targets, 8.9 ppg). The 12.0 aDOT gives big-play juice but the week-to-week floor is near zero. Now on a new team in a thin Miami corps, he could recapture peripheral targets. Ceiling is streamable spike weeks; floor is undraftable. The volatility makes him a bench flier only.

cooper kupp.verdict: Aging but still commands 16% targets and 76% snaps — safe PPR floor, muted ceiling
cooper kupp.report: High-volume, fading-efficiency: 16.0% target share, 0.34 WOPR and 76% snaps kept him relevant at 6.8 ppg, but the 7.5 aDOT and age-33 profile signal decline. He's the clear No. 2 behind JSN in Seattle with Shaheed pushing. Ceiling is a steady WR4 if health holds all 17; floor is a bench PPR body if usage slips further. Reliable volume makes him a fine bye-week fill.

caleb douglas.verdict: Rookie WR3 with zero data — deep-league name only
caleb douglas.report: No usage or efficiency to grade; a rookie sitting third on Miami's chart behind Wease and Washington. Any value is speculative on attrition. Ceiling is a late-season emergence if the room keeps thinning; floor is a healthy scratch. Not a redraft consideration.

kayshon boutte.verdict: Elite per-target efficiency (2.63 EPA/g, 17 aDOT) but A.J. Brown's arrival threatens the volume
kayshon boutte.report: Low-to-mid volume, elite efficiency: 21.5% air-yards share, 17.0 aDOT and a huge 2.63 rec EPA/g show he wins downfield, and 7.3 ppg on modest targets is impressive. The concern is the depth chart — A.J. Brown and Doubs now sit ahead, squeezing his 12% target share lower. Ceiling is a big-play WR3 if he holds the LWR role; floor is a fade if targets dry up. Talent is real; opportunity got worse.

brandon aiyuk.verdict: Projected zero and not reporting — undraftable until his status clears
brandon aiyuk.report: A 2026 projection of 0 and a DNR/injury flag mean there's no expected role to grade; his 2024 line (3.7 ppg on 47 targets) was already a down year cut short. Until he's healthy and on a defined depth chart, there's no case. Ceiling is a mid-season buy-low if he returns to form; floor is a lost season. Do not spend a pick.

ja'kobi lane.verdict: Rookie WR3 behind Flowers and Bateman — camp buzz only, no data
ja'kobi lane.report: No NFL usage to interpret; a rookie third on Baltimore's chart behind Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman. The training-camp update is generic and gives no concrete depth-chart shift. Ceiling is a late-season role if Bateman slips; floor is inactive. Monitor camp reps but don't draft in standard leagues.

ted hurst iii.verdict: Undrafted-type rookie with no depth-chart match — pure deep-league flier
ted hurst iii.report: No usage data and no confirmed roster spot in Tampa's receiver room. There is nothing to grade beyond a modest projection. Ceiling is a camp surprise earning a rotational role; floor is the practice squad. Ignore in all but the deepest dynasty formats.

keon coleman.verdict: Strong 0.41 WOPR and air-yards share, but DJ Moore's arrival crowds an already thin room
keon coleman.report: High-volume, decent-efficiency when on the field: 16.7% target share, 22.8% air-yards share and 0.41 WOPR at 11.2 aDOT are genuinely good. But Buffalo added DJ Moore atop Shakir and Palmer, threatening his target base and dropping him to WR4 on paper. Ceiling is a boom WR3 if he wins the outside job; floor is TD-dependent volatility (6.0 ppg). The talent flashes; the competition is the risk.

dontayvion wicks.verdict: Camp reports peg him Philly's WR2 with standout reps — real opportunity opening behind DeVonta Smith
dontayvion wicks.report: Modest GB volume (12.8% target share, 1.09 rec EPA/g) undersells the new signal: camp notes place him as Philadelphia's WR2 behind DeVonta Smith with the team's standout catches and a Keenan Allen comp from the staff. That's a concrete opening in a high-powered offense. Ceiling is a low-end WR3 if the role holds; floor is a rotational piece if Lemon or Brown push back. Start taking him rounds 13-14 on the camp momentum.

savion williams.verdict: Gadget usage at 12% snaps and 2.6% target share — no path to volume in a full room
savion williams.report: Low-volume, mixed-efficiency gadget: 2.6% target share, 0.04 WOPR and just 12% snaps, with a negative rush EPA. The touches are manufactured, not earned, and Green Bay's room (Watson, Reed, Golden) leaves no runway. Ceiling is occasional trick-play spike weeks; floor is fantasy irrelevance. Not draftable outside best-ball.

pat bryant.verdict: Positive rec EPA on real air-yards share, but Waddle's arrival buries him in Denver
pat bryant.report: Low-to-mid volume, solid efficiency: 11.0% target share, 16.2% air-yards share and 1.09 rec EPA/g on 48% snaps as a rookie is encouraging. The 'need a chance' feature fits, but Denver's room now has Sutton, Waddle and Franklin ahead, making the fourth-target path narrow. Ceiling is a bye-week streamer if injuries hit; floor is a bench stash. Talent flashed but opportunity shrank.

tory horton.verdict: Elite efficiency on 8 games (2.96 pts/tgt, 15.3 aDOT) with aging Kupp ahead — real breakout runway
tory horton.report: Low-volume, elite-efficiency quadrant: in 8 games he posted 2.96 pts/tgt, 15.3 aDOT, 0.28 WOPR and 1.28 rec EPA/g — a downfield profile that only needs targets. Seattle's No. 3 role sits behind a 33-year-old Kupp and Shaheed, both attrition risks. Ceiling is a WR3 if he seizes snaps midseason; floor is a rotational deep threat. Start taking him rounds 13-14 as the efficiency edge and opening ahead are clear.

elijah sarratt.verdict: Rookie WR4 in a set Baltimore room — no data, no path
elijah sarratt.report: No NFL usage to grade; fourth on Baltimore's chart behind Flowers, Bateman and Lane. There is no volume or efficiency signal and no clear opening. Ceiling is a depth emergence late; floor is inactive. Deep-dynasty only.

dyami brown.verdict: Five years of low production, now buried behind McLaurin and Diggs — fade
dyami brown.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency: 9.9% target share, -0.19 rec EPA/g and just 37% snaps despite a 14.0 aDOT, and the career arc (2.9 ppg in 2025) is flat. Washington added Stefon Diggs atop McLaurin, dropping him to a clear WR4. Ceiling is spot deep-shot weeks; floor is off the fantasy radar. No reason to draft.

darius slayton.verdict: 81% snaps and 25% air-yards share give a real deep-threat floor behind Nabers
darius slayton.report: Mid-volume, steady-efficiency: 15.5% target share, a big 25.0% air-yards share, 0.41 WOPR and 81% snaps with 1.29 rec EPA/g make him a reliable field-stretcher. He's the clear No. 2 behind Malik Nabers with Mooney and aging OBJ around. Ceiling is a low-end WR3 in spike weeks; floor is a boom/bust deep threat (5.8 ppg). TD-dependent but the snap and air-yards volume are dependable.

treylon burks.verdict: WR8 on the chart with -1.10 rec EPA/g — no volume, no efficiency, fade
treylon burks.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency: 12.5% target share in a tiny 8-game sample but a dismal -1.10 rec EPA/g, and he's now eighth on Washington's depth behind McLaurin, Diggs, Antonio Williams and Dyami Brown. There is no realistic path to targets. Ceiling is emergency depth; floor is a healthy scratch. Undraftable in redraft.

tyquan thornton.verdict: Extreme deep threat (26.9 aDOT, 2.19 EPA/g) but 9% targets behind Rice and Worthy — boom/bust
tyquan thornton.report: Low-volume, elite-per-target: a 26.9 aDOT, 27.5% air-yards share and 2.19 rec EPA/g on only a 9% target share make him a pure field-stretcher, capable of big spike weeks (2.18 pts/tgt). But Kansas City's room (Rice, Worthy, Royals) leaves him a No. 3/4 at 39% snaps. Ceiling is a few explosive TD games; floor is many zeros. A best-ball/deep-league dart, not a lineup staple.

andrei iosivas.verdict: WR3 in a top-heavy CIN room; 76% snaps give a pulse but 10% target share caps him
andrei iosivas.report: Low-volume, decent-efficiency quadrant: 76% snap share but only 10.2% target share and 0.24 WOPR behind Chase and Higgins. 2024's 120 pts was largely TD-fueled (3.33 pts/touch) and cratered to 90 as scores dried up. Floor is a benchable WR5; ceiling only opens on a Higgins injury. Playoff slate (@CAR, @IND, BAL) is neutral. A last-round contingency stash, nothing more.

jahan dotson.verdict: Buried WR3 in ATL with negative receiving EPA and shrinking snaps — a fade
jahan dotson.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency quadrant and no path: 8.3% target share, 57% snaps, and a brutal -1.00 rec EPA/g despite a 15.4 aDOT. He sits behind London and Branch with production trending down two straight years (2.5 then 3.0 PPG). Ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead; floor is off the fantasy radar. No reason to draft outside deep dynasty.

marvin mims jr..verdict: Explosive gadget/returner whose value hinges on TDs and big plays, not volume
marvin mims jr..report: Boom-bust profile: 51 targets plus 12 carries with a high weekly stdev (8.6 in 2024). Efficiency is big-play driven (9.7 yds/tgt in 2024) but 2025 dipped to 6.3 as the role narrowed. Low 9.9% target share means he's TD- and return-dependent, not a steady producer. Ceiling is a few explosion weeks; floor is single-digit blanks. Fine as a bench flier late.

kavontae turpin.verdict: Dual-threat gadget in DAL with efficient touches but a 35% snap ceiling
kavontae turpin.report: Low-volume, efficient quadrant: 26 catches plus 17 carries and strong 10.4 yds/tgt with a glowing 1.11 rec EPA/g, but a 35% snap share and 6.9% target share behind Lamb and Pickens cap the ceiling. Value comes from manufactured touches and return scores, keeping variance high. Floor is streaky WR5; ceiling needs an injury to the top two. A late dart only.

jaylin lane.verdict: Year-1 slot buried at WR6 in WSH behind McLaurin and Diggs — no volume path
jaylin lane.report: Low-volume with negative rec EPA (-0.38): 8.3% target share on just 36% snaps and only 10 first downs. The 13.3 aDOT hints at a downfield role but the depth chart (McLaurin, Diggs, Williams, Brown ahead) offers no clear opening. Floor is irrelevant; ceiling requires multiple injuries. Skip outside the deepest leagues.

demario douglas.verdict: Elite per-target efficiency but AJ Brown's arrival gutted his snaps to 26%
demario douglas.report: High-efficiency, collapsing-volume story: his 1.76 rec EPA/g and 2.52 pts/touch are excellent, but snap share fell from a 2024 slot-workhorse role (66 catches, 148 pts) to just 26% behind A.J. Brown and Doubs. The talent is real; the opportunity vanished. Floor is a WR5 stash; ceiling only returns if Brown misses time. Tough playoff draw (@KC). Monitor, don't draft.

devaughn vele.verdict: Strong per-target metrics but a crowded NO room and weak QB cap the upside
devaughn vele.report: When on the field he flashed real volume: 13.3% target share, 0.33 WOPR and a huge 1.87 rec EPA/g over 9 games. But he's now WR4 in New Orleans behind Olave and rookie Tyson with a shaky QB situation, and 2025 was injury-shortened (9 of 13 played). Efficiency edge is genuine; the path to targets isn't. Floor low, ceiling if Olave misses time. Late stash.

nick westbrook-ikhine.verdict: 2024's 136 pts was TD mirage (4.24 pts/touch); 2025 collapse exposes it
nick westbrook-ikhine.report: Textbook TD-dependence: 2024's 136 points came on a wildly unsustainable 4.24 pts/touch, and when the scores stopped he cratered to 20 points on a 5.2% target share and 0.11 WOPR. Now WR3 behind Pierce and Downs. Floor is a zero; ceiling needs both a role and red-zone luck to return. Not worth a pick.

ashton dulin.verdict: Deep-only role with 2.7% target share — pure special-teams dart
ashton dulin.report: Tiny-volume, big-play profile: 15.8 aDOT and flashy per-catch numbers but only 10 targets and a 0.07 WOPR on 21% snaps as WR4 in Indy. Nothing here suggests a fantasy role even in a full injury scenario. Floor and ceiling both negligible. Undraftable outside 20-team formats.

tutu atwell.verdict: New team, deep-threat role, WR6 on the depth chart — a lottery ticket
tutu atwell.report: Field-stretcher with a 20.1 aDOT but almost no volume in 2025 (15 targets, 8 games, 0.14 WOPR) after a modest 99-point 2024. Now in Miami sitting sixth behind Wease and Washington. The efficiency is boom-bust and the target path is unclear on a new team. Floor near zero; ceiling only if he wins a starting deep role in camp. Wait-and-see.

kevin coleman jr..verdict: Rookie with no pro data and no clear depth-chart foothold in MIA — blind dart
kevin coleman jr..report: No NFL usage to evaluate and no Sleeper depth match, so opportunity is purely speculative in a Miami room being reshuffled. Any value would come from a camp surge no data yet confirms. Floor is a non-factor; ceiling depends entirely on winning targets we can't project. Draft only as a final-round stash in deep leagues.

hollywood brown.verdict: Proven when targeted (138 pts) but new team and a crowded PHI room cloud volume
hollywood brown.report: His 2025 rebound to 138 points on 74 targets shows he can produce with a real role, and 1.86 pts/tgt is fine. But moving to Philadelphia puts him behind A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith with volume far from guaranteed, and his career has swung wildly year to year. Floor is a boom-bust WR5; ceiling needs an injury ahead. Speed profile keeps him TD-reliant. Late flier.

troy franklin.verdict: Scored 177 with a 0.47 WOPR yet priced as a dart — massive market mistake
troy franklin.report: High-volume, ascending quadrant and the clear value of this tier: 18.2% target share, 28% air-yards share and an elite 0.47 WOPR drove 177 points (10.4 PPG) in a true breakout year. The ADP of 171 bakes in heavy regression from Waddle's arrival, but even a shared role beats this cost badly. Floor is a usable flex; ceiling is low-end WR2. Start taking him rounds 8-9, not the last round.

kendrick bourne.verdict: Veteran slot with a real 0.27 WOPR and 1.47 rec EPA — quiet floor play
kendrick bourne.report: Low-to-mid volume, solid efficiency: 10.8% target share, 0.27 WOPR and a strong 1.47 rec EPA/g over 14 games, plus 27 first downs. As ARI's slot behind Harrison and Wilson he has a defined if modest role. Floor is a bye-week fill-in; ceiling is a handful of WR3 weeks if Harrison draws coverage. High weekly variance (6.6 stdev). Depth-league value.

kalif raymond.verdict: Efficient short-area gadget/returner but 6% target share on a new CHI role
kalif raymond.report: Low-volume, efficient profile: 2.23 pts/tgt and strong YAC (6.5) but just a 6.0% target share and 5.6 aDOT keep the ceiling tiny as WR4 in Chicago behind Odunze and Burden. Production is TD- and return-leveraged with a 4.5 weekly stdev. Floor negligible; ceiling a rare spike week. Not a draftable target.

luke mccaffrey.verdict: Tiny sample of great efficiency but WR7 in WSH — no realistic volume
luke mccaffrey.report: His 3.42 pts/tgt and 13.5 yds/tgt on 15 targets flash talent, but the sample is minuscule and he sits seventh on the depth chart behind McLaurin, Diggs, Williams and Brown. There is simply no target path. Floor is a non-factor; ceiling requires an implausible cascade of injuries. Undraftable in standard formats.

joshua palmer.verdict: Declining role as BUF's WR3 behind Moore and Shakir — mostly a fade
joshua palmer.report: Volume trending the wrong way: dropped from 65 targets and 107 points in 2024 to 37 targets and 52 points in 2025, now WR3 in Buffalo behind DJ Moore and Shakir. Efficiency (8.2 yds/tgt) is fine but unspectacular. Floor is a benchable WR5; ceiling needs an injury and a Josh Allen bump. Deep-league contingency only.

cyrus allen.verdict: Rookie WR5 in KC, listed questionable — camp roundup gives no real signal
cyrus allen.report: No pro data and buried behind Rice, Worthy and others as a fifth-string rookie carrying a questionable tag. The cited news is a generic camp roundup with nothing specific, so it doesn't move the needle. Any value is purely speculative on a KC breakout that isn't evidenced yet. Floor negligible; ceiling only on multiple injuries. Skip.

skyler bell.verdict: Undrafted-tier rookie WR5 in BUF with no data and no target path
skyler bell.report: No NFL usage to grade and fifth on Buffalo's depth chart behind Moore, Shakir, Palmer and Coleman. There is no evidence of an opening or a camp surge. Floor and ceiling both non-factors barring a dramatic injury cascade. Not a draftable player in standard formats.

bryce lance.verdict: Rookie WR5 in a crowded NO room — pure deep-dynasty name
bryce lance.report: No pro production and fifth on New Orleans' chart behind Olave, Tyson, Means and Vele, with a shaky QB situation limiting the whole room's upside. Nothing in the data suggests a 2026 role. Floor irrelevant; ceiling requires injuries and a leap we can't yet forecast. Undraftable outside dynasty stashes.

jordan whittington.verdict: Fourth wheel in a loaded LAR room with cratering efficiency; pure roster filler.
jordan whittington.report: Low-volume, low-efficiency quadrant: 5.1% target share, 0.10 WOPR, 41% snaps, and PPG fell from 3.1 to 2.1 as air-yards share dropped to 3.8%. Buried behind Nacua, Adams, and rookie/Mumpfield competition, he needs multiple injuries to matter. Floor is a zero every week; ceiling only opens on a Nacua/Adams absence. No draftable path.

zavion thomas.verdict: Rookie WR5 on a crowded Bears depth chart with no NFL usage to project.
zavion thomas.report: No pro sample to lean on, and the depth chart is a wall: Odunze, Burden, and Walker sit ahead as the listed SWR #5. Ceiling depends entirely on injuries plus a camp climb we have no evidence of. Floor is inactive weeks. A dart with no data supporting a target-share path; leave on the wire.

odell beckham jr..verdict: Aging name with 2024's 1.1 PPG and 3.1 yds/tgt; the profile is finished.
odell beckham jr..report: Last real sample showed 18 targets, 9 catches, 0.81 pts/tgt — low-volume, low-efficiency fade quadrant, the worst combination. No 2025 usage and no clear role. Ceiling is a nostalgia spike week or two; floor is out of the rotation entirely. Nothing in the data supports rostering.

devontez walker.verdict: Elite deep-ball efficiency (24.5 aDOT, 2.24 rec EPA/g) on a sliver of volume, but fully buried.
devontez walker.report: Low-volume/high-efficiency profile: only 8 targets but 17 yds/tgt and monster EPA on a 24.5 aDOT — a big-play specialist. Problem is opportunity: WR5 behind Flowers, Bateman, Lane, and Sarratt at 25% snaps. TD-dependent boom weeks are possible, but the target path is nonexistent barring injuries. Watchlist only.

malachi fields.verdict: Rookie listed WR6 in NY behind Nabers, Mooney, Slayton — no route to volume.
malachi fields.report: No pro usage exists, and he's the sixth option on his own depth chart. Ceiling requires a cascade of injuries just to see the field, and there's no efficiency sample to argue talent will force snaps. Floor is inactive. Undraftable in a 12-team format.

xavier hutchinson.verdict: Real 2025 leap (11.2% tgt share, 0.26 WOPR) makes him the best contingency bet in this tier.
xavier hutchinson.report: Moved into the moderate-volume/solid-efficiency zone: 57 targets, 5.8 PPG, 21 first downs, 57% snaps and productive rec EPA — a genuine step up from 2024's 1.4 PPG. The catch is a crowded room (Collins, Higgins, Dell, Noel), so his standalone role is capped. But Houston's WRs get hurt, and his usage shows he'd absorb targets. Best late flier here; start considering after pick 150.

dont'e thornton jr..verdict: Huge air-yards share but -1.09 rec EPA/g — volume that hurt the offense is at risk.
dont'e thornton jr..report: He commanded a 24.9% air-yards share and 16.6 aDOT, but the -1.09 rec EPA and 0.78 pts/tgt scream inefficiency on deep looks — high air-yards, poor conversion, the kind of role that gets reassigned. Ceiling is a couple of long-TD weeks; floor is losing snaps outright. Fade unless the role expands with better output.

olamide zaccheaus.verdict: Veteran volume (14.7% tgt share) but negative EPA and a shrinking role behind London and youth.
olamide zaccheaus.report: Moderate-volume/poor-efficiency: 65 targets and 0.30 WOPR but -0.27 rec EPA and just 4.8 yds/tgt, and PPG slid from 6.6 to 5.0. Now the SWR #4 with Branch and Dotson in the mix, his target base looks likely to erode. Floor is steady low-end depth; ceiling is a WR5 bye-week fill. Not a target early.

chimere dike.verdict: 126 rookie points on real volume, but Tennessee's rebuilt room threatens the snaps.
chimere dike.report: Encouraging rookie usage: 74 targets, 11 carries, 0.31 WOPR, 59% snaps, 7.4 PPG — moderate volume with league-average efficiency. The forward risk is the depth chart adding Tate, Ridley, and Robinson, pushing him to SWR #5, so his 2025 role isn't guaranteed. Ceiling if he holds the slot is a low-end flex; floor is a rotational piece. Speculative.

isaiah bond.verdict: Deep-role volume (21.4% air-yards) but flat EPA and a new, crowded Cleveland room.
isaiah bond.report: Low-to-moderate volume/mediocre efficiency: 9.3% target share, 17.1 aDOT, but essentially neutral rec EPA and 1.24 pts/tgt. Now behind Jeudy with young additions competing, his path is murky on a shaky offense. Boom weeks are TD-reliant; floor is spotty usage. Wire-level flier.

konata mumpfield.verdict: Tiny role (6.2% tgt share, -0.88 EPA) as the LAR WR4; no case here.
konata mumpfield.report: Low-volume, negative-efficiency fade: 23 targets, 1.5 PPG, 32% snaps and a poor rec EPA. Stuck behind Nacua, Adams, and Whittington, he has no realistic target path. Floor is inactive; ceiling is a fluky spot start. Not draftable.

mack hollins.verdict: Strong 2025 usage (16.2% tgt, 1.94 EPA/g) collapses now that A.J. Brown headlines New England.
mack hollins.report: Last year he was moderate-volume/good-efficiency: 65 targets, 0.39 WOPR, 28 first downs, elite rec EPA on 68% snaps. But the room reshuffled with Brown, Doubs, and Boutte, dropping him toward RWR #5 — the volume that drove his value is likely gone. The camp headline is generic and non-informative. Floor is depth; ceiling needs an injury ahead. Fade the reputation.

brenen thompson.verdict: Rookie WR4 on the Chargers with no usage to project; deep dart only.
brenen thompson.report: No NFL sample and a depth chart headed by McConkey, Johnston, and Harris leave no clear role. Ceiling is speed-based long TDs if he climbs the chart; there's no data to bet on it yet. Floor is inactive. Leave for waivers.

keandre lambert-smith.verdict: Deep aDOT but 3.6% target share and 19% snaps; nowhere near fantasy relevance.
keandre lambert-smith.report: Low-volume/negative-efficiency: 12 targets, 0.9 PPG, -0.49 rec EPA even on a 17.6 aDOT. As LWR #5 behind McConkey, Johnston, and Harris, opportunity is nonexistent. Ceiling is a garbage-time deep ball; floor is inactive. Undraftable.

kyle williams.verdict: Eye-popping per-touch efficiency (4.10 pts/touch, 19 aDOT) trapped behind A.J. Brown and Doubs.
kyle williams.report: Textbook low-volume/high-efficiency: only 21 targets but 2.34 pts/tgt, positive rec EPA, big aDOT — talent flashing on scraps. The opening isn't there, though: SWR #6 behind Brown, Doubs, and Boutte at 31% snaps. He needs injuries to convert that efficiency into volume. Intriguing profile, no current path; stash only in deep leagues.

tez johnson.verdict: Efficient rookie slot (1.09 rec EPA/g) but Questionable tag and a deep Tampa chart cap him.
tez johnson.report: Moderate efficiency on light volume: 44 targets, 0.23 WOPR, 5.4 PPG with positive rec EPA and added rushing usage — productive per snap. He's listed RWR #7 behind Egbuka, Godwin, and McMillan and carries a Questionable tag, so both health and opportunity are concerns. Godwin's age could crack the door. Late-round flier with real efficiency if snaps come.

jimmy horn jr..verdict: Dual-use rookie gadget snaps but 6.4% tgt share and 6.0 aDOT limit the ceiling.
jimmy horn jr..report: Low-volume utility profile: 15 targets, 8 carries, positive rush EPA, but a shallow 6.0 aDOT and tiny target share cap upside. As a rookie with no clear route to volume, he's a manufactured-touch dart. Ceiling is a rushing-TD spike week; floor is invisible. Deep-league only.

mitchell tinsley.verdict: 8-game 25% snap role in Cincinnati; not enough volume to matter.
mitchell tinsley.report: Low-volume/marginal-efficiency: 24 targets, 8 catches, 1.9 PPG on 25% snaps in a limited eight-game window. No depth-chart data suggests a bigger role is coming behind Cincinnati's established options. Ceiling is a spot deep TD; floor is inactive. Off-radar.

calvin austin iii.verdict: Real air-yards role (25.5%, 0.37 WOPR) but a new team stacks him behind Nabers and Mooney.
calvin austin iii.report: Moderate-volume vertical role: 55 targets, 25.5% air-yards share, 0.37 WOPR, though efficiency slipped (-0.30 rec EPA, PPG down 7.0 to 5.1). Now projected as a Giants WR4 behind Nabers, Mooney, and Slayton, his 2024-25 target base won't transfer. Ceiling needs an injury ahead; floor is depth. Speculative new-team stash.

jalen royals.verdict: Thin KC WR room behind Rice/Worthy gives a second-year flier genuine breakout upside.
jalen royals.report: Near-zero 2025 sample (2 games, negative EPA in noise), so this is an opportunity bet, not a data one: Kansas City's room is thin behind Rice and Worthy, both of whom carry availability risk, and Royals sits atop the unproven group. In Mahomes' offense a WR3 role has real flex value. Floor is inactive; ceiling is startable if the door opens. Take a shot in the final rounds.

anthony gould.verdict: Sixth WR with 0.5% target share and negative air-yards; pure practice-squad filler, not draftable
anthony gould.report: Low volume + poor efficiency, the clear fade quadrant: 9% snaps over 11 games, 0.5% target share, 0 first downs and negative receiving EPA. As the #6 SWR behind Pierce, Downs, NWI and Dulin there is no realistic path to touches. Ceiling requires multiple injuries ahead of him; floor is zero fantasy relevance. Undraftable in 12-team leagues.

greg dortch.verdict: Veteran slot filler at 4.4 PPG buried behind St. Brown, Williams and TeSlaa; no standalone value
greg dortch.report: Low volume, mediocre efficiency: 6.8% target share, 34% snaps, 2.09 pts/touch and only 6.2 yds/target. Production dipped from 90 to 75 points year over year and he's the #4 WR in a room fronted by St. Brown. Floor is bench fodder; ceiling needs an injury cascade to unlock any weekly usable line. Only a deep-league desperation dart.

elic ayomanor.verdict: Proven 18.5% target share and 0.50 WOPR as a rookie, but brutal efficiency and a suddenly crowded room
elic ayomanor.report: High volume + poor efficiency, a warning profile: 89 targets, 32.5% air-yards share and 0.50 WOPR are startable-level opportunity, but -0.60 receiving EPA/g and 1.31 pts/target say the volume produced little. The bigger risk is the depth chart now listing him #4 behind Tate, Wan'Dale and Ridley, so the target share that made him interesting may evaporate. If he re-earns the alpha role the ceiling is real; if not he's a fade. Highest upside in this tier by far.

malik benson.verdict: Undrafted-caliber rookie #5 on the Raiders' WR chart with zero production baseline
malik benson.report: No NFL usage data to lean on, and the depth chart buries him at RWR #5 behind Tucker, Nailor, Bech and Thornton. Without a snap or target profile there's nothing to project forward beyond special-teams reps. Ceiling is a camp riser who forces his way onto the field; floor is inactive. Not a draft-worthy dart in standard formats.

isaiah williams.verdict: Low-aDOT slot at 3.9 PPG behind Garrett Wilson; efficiency ordinary, ceiling capped
isaiah williams.report: Low volume, average efficiency: 8.8% target share, 36% snaps and a 3.4 aDOT that limits upside to dink-and-dunk PPR points at best. The 11 first downs on 26 catches are fine but the profile screams matchup-dependent depth. With Wilson entrenched and Mitchell added, the path to volume is narrow. Floor is bench; ceiling needs injuries ahead of him.

bo melton.verdict: Deep-shot decoy at 1.4 PPG in a crowded Packers room; no volume to speak of
bo melton.report: Low volume, thin efficiency: 4% target share, 10% snaps and a 17.1 aDOT that makes him a boom-or-nothing field-stretcher with negative receiving EPA. Fifth on the depth chart behind Watson, Reed, Golden and Williams, he has no route to consistent targets. Ceiling is a random long-ball week; floor is total irrelevance. Not draftable.

ben skowronek.verdict: Blocking-role WR5 with 6 targets all season; roster clogger, not a fantasy asset
ben skowronek.report: Effectively no receiving volume: 1.4% target share, 4 catches on 6 targets, WOPR 0.04. The high pts/target is a small-sample artifact off almost no usage. Buried behind Metcalf, Pittman and Bernard, he's a special-teams and blocking body. Floor and ceiling are both near replacement level in fantasy terms.

derius davis.verdict: Return specialist with 0.9% target share; gadget touches only, no receiving role
derius davis.report: Low volume, negligible impact: 2024 gave 40 points on gadget usage, but 2025 collapsed to 0.9% target share, 11% snaps and 0 first downs. As the #6 slot behind McConkey, Johnston and Harris he's a returner first. Ceiling is a few designed touches per game; floor is fantasy zero. Undraftable outside deep return-yardage formats.

xavier smith.verdict: Tiny sample with elite 1.37 EPA/g but zero path behind Nacua, Adams and Whittington
xavier smith.report: Low volume + strong efficiency, the classic breakout profile if opportunity opened: 16.9 aDOT, 12.6 yds/target and a standout 1.37 receiving EPA/g on 24 targets. The problem is the Rams' room is jammed with Nacua and Adams ahead of him, so the efficiency has no volume to scale into. Ceiling requires two injuries; floor is deep-league bench. Worth a late watch, not a pick.

tyrell shavers.verdict: On PUP with intriguing 1.12 EPA/g and 0.20 WOPR, but health and depth both block him
tyrell shavers.report: Low volume + good efficiency: 7.7% target share, 12.3% air-yards share, 13.0 aDOT and 1.12 receiving EPA/g show real per-target juice on limited work. But he opens on PUP and sits #6 in a room behind Moore, Shakir, Palmer and Coleman, so both availability and opportunity are against him. Ceiling depends on health plus injuries ahead; floor is missed time. Monitor, don't draft.

colbie young.verdict: Rookie WR5 stuck behind Chase and Higgins; no data and no realistic target path
colbie young.report: No usage baseline as a rookie, and the depth chart is unforgiving: fifth in a room fronted by Chase and Higgins who command the vast majority of targets. Even a strong camp leaves scraps in this offense. Ceiling is deep-injury contingency in a high-powered passing attack; floor is inactive. Not a draftable name in standard leagues.

barion brown.verdict: Rookie #8 on the depth chart; camp roundup is generic and adds nothing to a bare profile
barion brown.report: No production data and the deepest slot listed here at SWR #8 behind Olave, Tyson, Means and Vele. The July camp headline is a generic team roundup with no player-specific intel, so it moves nothing. Ceiling is a special-teams-plus-gadget rookie who flashes; floor is roster cut. Undraftable given both the depth and lack of any signal.

trey mcbride.verdict: Elite volume TE1 — 27.9% target share and 169 looks are real, but a TD spike and QB downgrade cap the ceiling
trey mcbride.report: High-volume/good-efficiency quadrant: 169 targets, 27.9% share, 0.59 WOPR, 91% snaps — league-most routes at TE. That volume is the safest floor at the position. Ceiling case is a repeat of 316 pts; floor case is the 12.5 PPG he posted without Brissett, plus TD regression from 11 (year totals 1-3-2-11) and added competition. Market and Smyth both flag the round-2 price vs Bowers. Still the closest thing to a locked TE1.

brock bowers.verdict: Elite bounce-back — 2024's 263-pt line and top red-zone share say the down 2025 was injury, not decline
brock bowers.report: High-volume/good-efficiency talent: 23.4% share, 0.53 WOPR, highest RZ target share at TE, and 16+ PPG in games he didn't leave early. 2024 gave 263 pts; 2025 fell to 176 across just 12 healthy games. Ceiling is TE1 overall on Kubiak's creative usage with almost no other Raiders pass-catchers; floor is another injury-shortened year. Mayer exists but doesn't threaten his target monopoly. Draft with confidence at his slight discount to McBride.

colston loveland.verdict: Late-rookie surge is the whole thesis — 20 PPG and 80% route share down the stretch point to a real leap
colston loveland.report: Low-to-mid volume/strong-efficiency breakout: 16.6% share and 65% snaps overall, but once handed full snaps he closed at ~20 PPG on 12 targets/game and 2.63 YPRR. 8.7 yds/tgt and 2.80 pts/touch show the per-route talent. Ceiling is a genuine top-5 TE if the late-year role holds; floor is a return to the split-time early-season usage. Kmet coexists — Chicago runs the most 2-TE sets in the NFL — and DJ Moore's exit opens red-zone work.

tyler warren.verdict: Rock-steady sophomore — 21.5% target share and a 4.7 weekly stdev give the safest floor outside the top tier
tyler warren.report: High-volume/modest-efficiency quadrant: 112 targets and 21.5% share as a rookie, with a tiny 4.7 weekly stdev — remarkably consistent. Efficiency (1.68 pts/tgt, 5.4 aDOT) is capped by a short-area role and shaky QB play. Ceiling grows if Steichen's 'offensive weapon' gadget usage plus Pittman's exit push his targets-per-route (already jumped 21%→30% without Pittman); floor is the weekly-reliable low-end TE1 he already was. Bad TD luck should correct.

kyle pitts sr..verdict: Bounce-back to 12.4 PPG restored some trust, but efficiency and TD volatility keep the ceiling in check
kyle pitts sr..report: Mid-volume/average-efficiency profile: 118 targets and 12.4 PPG in 2025 nearly doubled the miserable 2024 line (7.7 PPG). 7.9 yds/tgt is fine, not special, and the 9.6 weekly stdev is high. Ceiling is a low-end TE1 if the target volume holds; floor is another quiet, TD-starved year like 2024. No advanced-usage or depth data provided, so I'm leaning on the raw target count, which at least confirms real opportunity. Fringe starter at a fair price.

harold fannin jr..verdict: Elite per-route rookie on a bad offense — the one profile where a great TE still produces through the muck
harold fannin jr..report: High-volume/modest-scoring quadrant: 107 targets, 21.8% share, No. 1 among TEs in targets per route as a rookie, with the most avoided tackles by a TE since 2020. Efficiency in points (1.74/tgt) is dragged down by Cleveland's dead offense, not talent. Ceiling is a top-6 finish if the Slowik/Monken TE-heavy scheme feeds him; floor is capped by Njoku (saw 9 tgt/game in the 4 Njoku missed) and QB chaos. ADP 76 is inside the top 100, so priced, not a sleeper.

sam laporta.verdict: Bounce-back bet — elite YAC and per-target efficiency on a great offense, if health and volume return
sam laporta.report: Note: depth chart and NFC-North playoff slate confirm he's still in Detroit, so the Arizona-move reasoning is stale. Low-volume/strong-efficiency last year: only 49 targets across an injury-shortened 9-game core (2.18 pts/tgt, 10.0 yds/tgt, No. 1 TE in YAC/rec). 2024 gave 175 pts on 83 targets. Ceiling is a return to that low-end TE1 role in Detroit's offense; floor is the injury-plagued 6.3 PPG of 2025. Buy the efficiency and hope volume climbs.

george kittle.verdict: Best per-target TE alive, but PUP, an Achilles, and age 32-33 make the floor terrifying
george kittle.report: Low-volume/elite-efficiency profile: 2.34 pts/tgt and 9.1 yds/tgt on just 69 targets, 4.21 rec EPA/g — still No. 1 in nearly every rate stat. But he's on PUP off an early-season Achilles, YAC dipped for the first time, and he'll be 33. Ceiling if healthy is a top-3 TE that his 2024 (237 pts) proves; floor is games missed and diminished burst. A boom-bust dart, not a set-and-forget starter — grab Tonges as insurance.

tucker kraft.verdict: Freakish YAC monster on six targets, but an ACL and Green Bay's slow ramp cloud the games he'll play
tucker kraft.report: Low-volume/elite-efficiency quadrant: 2.66 pts/tgt, 11.1 yds/tgt, 3.55 pts/touch, 4.89 rec EPA/g — he devours yards after the catch on tiny volume (44 targets in 8 games). That's exactly the skill an ACL recovery and an ease-in period blunt. Ceiling is a low-end TE1 if fully healthy; floor is a delayed, limited return. Camp intel is positive but Green Bay is historically cautious. Talent is real; the timeline is the risk.

dallas goedert.verdict: Fine punt starter — TD-inflated 2025, but AJ Brown's exit and a steady role keep him usable
dallas goedert.report: Mid-volume/TD-boosted quadrant: 82 targets, 20.8% share, but 2.26 pts/tgt on only 7.2 yds/tgt screams touchdown reliance — 2024's healthy-but-quiet 6.1 PPG shows the downside. Ceiling is a repeat TE5-6 line if the scoring holds and Brown's departure funnels red-zone looks; floor is the TD regression the market is already pricing (going as a low-end TE). Stowers is no real rookie threat. A last-resort starter you can likely replace off waivers.

travis kelce.verdict: Age 37 and three straight down years — reliable targets but a shrinking, TD-starved ceiling
travis kelce.report: High-volume/fading-efficiency quadrant: still 108 targets and 20% share, but 1.79 pts/tgt and a 28th-ranked red-zone share as the lone option scream decline. Mahomes off an ACL matters — Kelce led TEs in points on Mahomes scrambles. Ceiling is a stable low-end TE1 if Rice/Worthy draw coverage off him; floor is continued erosion at 37 with more mouths (Rice full season, Walker) to feed. Volume gives a floor; the age curve caps everything above it.

jake ferguson.verdict: Pure Lamb-injury handcuff — TE1 overall without CeeDee, TE20 with him and Pickens healthy
jake ferguson.report: High-volume-when-available but role-dependent: 102 targets and 11.1 PPG overall, yet the split is stark — TE1 overall in games CeeDee Lamb missed, TE20 when Lamb played. Low aDOT (4.7), 8.9% air-yards share and 67% snaps show a checkdown role. Ceiling requires a Lamb absence; floor with Lamb and Pickens both healthy is fringe-startable at best. Draft him as insurance/upside on Dallas' passing chaos, not as a weekly plug-in.

mark andrews.verdict: TD-rebound dart with Likely gone and Lamar back, but the efficiency collapse is the loud warning
mark andrews.report: Mid-volume/poor-efficiency quadrant: 17.1% share, 0.09 rec EPA/g, last among NFL TEs in YAC and weak per-route even with Lamar — a red flag that the volume itself is fragile. RotoWire's rebound call leans on 11 TDs the last time his QB was healthy, i.e. pure TD variance. The opening is real (Likely gone, only Flowers competing), so I note it, but the usage contradicts a full sleeper endorsement. Ceiling is TD-fueled TE1 weeks; floor is another quiet year.

t.j. hockenson.verdict: Sleeper on QB upgrade — a healthy McCarthy is the opportunity his 2025 volume was starved of
t.j. hockenson.report: Low-volume/modest-efficiency quadrant: 15.9% share, 5.0 aDOT, 66 targets — his ceiling was strangled by disastrous QB play. RotoWire's call ties the down year to that, and a real QB upgrade is the lever. Ceiling is a return toward his old low-end TE1 form; floor is more short, low-value targets. At ADP 133 (outside top 100) the realistic upside clears the cost — start taking him in the last few TE rounds as your streamer with weekly upside.

kenyon sadiq.verdict: Rookie hybrid dart with zero pro data and Mason Taylor ahead — a dynasty/deep-league flyer only
kenyon sadiq.report: No NFL usage to grade, so I'm inferring from role and depth only: ESPN flags a hybrid WR/TE deployment, but Mason Taylor is the entrenched receiving TE and Sadiq is listed questionable. That's a crowded, unproven path in a weak Jets offense. Ceiling is a surprise gadget role that flashes; floor is irrelevance. Despite ADP 133 being outside the top 100, the competition and total absence of data don't support a sleeper badge — pure lottery ticket.

isaiah likely.verdict: New-team upside shot — good per-route history, but Theo Johnson and Nabers cap the target path
isaiah likely.report: Low-volume/decent-efficiency profile: 2025 cratered to 3.6 PPG on 12% share even with Lamar, a brutal follow to 2024's 7.3 PPG. The bull case is situational — Giants paid him TE money to reunite with Harbaugh's staff — but Theo Johnson is established and Malik Nabers commands the targets. Ceiling is a low-end TE1 if he wins the role; floor is the near-invisible 2025. Understandable pure-upside dart, but the usable-volume path isn't clear enough to badge as a sleeper.

dalton kincaid.verdict: Sleeper — Kittle-level per-route efficiency; the only thing missing is route share, which can climb
dalton kincaid.report: Low-volume/elite-efficiency quadrant: 2.57 pts/tgt, 11.7 yds/tgt, 3rd in NFL in yards per route before his injury — the talent is undeniable. The cap is Dawson Knox's run-blocking role limiting Kincaid's routes (37% snaps in 2025), but pre-injury he hit a career-high 60% route share and was TE6 when healthy. At ADP 136 (outside top 100), the ceiling as a young first-round TE in Buffalo's offense clears the price — start taking him as your final TE dart.

hunter henry.verdict: Everything broke right for TE14 — added Brown and Doubs, plus TD regression, sink the repeat
hunter henry.report: High-volume/TD-inflated quadrant: 87 targets, 17.4% share, but the production leaned on the most busted-coverage points in the NFL and the 6th-most red-zone targets of ANY player — and he still only finished TE14. Now New England adds Romeo Doubs and AJ Brown, thinning both the target and red-zone pie. Ceiling is a repeat of 2025's 10.5 PPG; floor is a clear step back as the offense gets weapons. Going too early relative to the regression case.

terrance ferguson.verdict: Deep sleeper on talent and a great offense, but a crowded Rams TE room makes it a genuine dart
terrance ferguson.report: Low-volume/small-sample quadrant: 25 targets, 6.5% share, 18.6 aDOT deep role and just 37% snaps as a rookie — barely any usage to grade. The case is the offense and Stafford, plus Smyth's read that he's the most talented of the group and 8 TDs wouldn't shock. Ceiling is a surprise breakout if he wins the job; floor is buried behind Parkinson, Higbee and rookie Klare. At ADP 167 the upside beats the cost — a last-round flyer, so I'll badge it, but temper expectations given the room.

juwan johnson.verdict: Sleeper — a quietly steady 17.7% share and 10.6 PPG at a last-round price, with Fant the only threat
juwan johnson.report: Mid-volume/solid-consistency quadrant: 102 targets, 17.7% share, 8.7 yds/tgt and a low 4.7 weekly stdev — he was a reliable near-TE1 producer in 2025, up from 7.2 PPG in 2024. Noah Fant's arrival is the competition to watch, but Johnson held the receiving role. Ceiling is a repeat low-end TE1 line; floor is a Fant-driven timeshare in a weak Saints offense. At ADP 163 the steady target share is real value — take him as your final-round TE with a usable floor.

brenton strange.verdict: Ascending JAX TE1 with 75% snaps and a 0.32 WOPR — a stable streamer whose usage grew year over year.
brenton strange.report: Moderate-volume, solid-efficiency quadrant: 15.6% target share, WOPR 0.32, 1.97 pts/tgt, and EPA/g 2.61 all trended up from 2024. Floor is anchored by 75% snaps and the clear TE1 role. Ceiling is capped because Jacksonville spreads targets among many mouths, as noted. A safe late-round starter, but few paths to elite weeks. Playoff slate (@HOU, @DAL, WSH) is neutral.

pat freiermuth.verdict: 2024's 9.9 ppg collapsed to 6.7 as snaps fell to 50% — Washington eats into a shrinking role.
pat freiermuth.report: Volume fell hard: target share dropped to 11.3%, snap share to 50%, EPA/g to 1.55 — a warning the role itself is eroding. Efficiency stayed fine (2.10 pts/tgt) but he needs TDs to matter. Darnell Washington's rise pressures the passing snaps. The 2024 line shows the ceiling if targets return, but the trend points the wrong way. wk15 BAL playoff draw is tough.

dalton schultz.verdict: Best volume in this tier — 106 targets, 19.1% share, 0.39 WOPR — the safest floor of the group.
dalton schultz.report: High-volume, adequate-efficiency profile: 10.5 ppg on 106 targets, WOPR 0.39, EPA/g 2.16 — a genuine every-week option unlike most here. Floor is strong given secure TE1 role and 71% snaps with no real Houston TE competition. Ceiling limited by low aDOT (6.2) and thin TD rate, but volume alone plays. Undervalued relative to ADP 167. Playoff draw (@PHI, @GB) is rough but the targets travel.

gunnar helm.verdict: Year-2 leap bet on a rookie TE1, but 10.7% share and 0.24 EPA/g say the profile is thin so far.
gunnar helm.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency rookie line: 10.7% target share, WOPR 0.22, EPA/g just 0.24, aDOT 5.5 — dink-and-dunk usage. Ceiling is the classic second-year TE breakout as Tennessee's offense and Ward develop. Floor is soft; he was barely a starter's-worth in 2025. Thin TE room around him is the one clear positive. Speculative dart, not a set-and-forget play.

chig okonkwo.verdict: New Washington TE with a thin WR room and Daniels — receiver-type usage in line for a target bump.
chig okonkwo.report: Consistent 15% target share and receiver-role aDOT, but efficiency is modest (1.57 pts/tgt) and air-yards share tiny (8.7%) — a possession piece. The bull case: Washington's thin pass-catcher group and Daniels' scramble-drill funnel more looks his way, which the expert calls flag. Floor is a low-end starter; ceiling is a top-10 TE if targets climb. Start taking him in the last two rounds as a TE lottery ticket.

aj barner.verdict: 8.7 ppg was heavily TD-fueled on low air yards; Arroyo's emergence threatens the receiving role.
aj barner.report: High-touch, low-air-yards profile: 13.8% target share but aDOT 4.4 and 7.7% air-yards share — the 2.17 pts/tgt leans on red-zone scores that regress. 77% snaps and goal-line work give a floor. The real risk: teammate Elijah Arroyo is the buzz of Seattle camp and could siphon the receiving snaps. Ceiling needs the TD rate to hold. TD-dependent tag fits.

oronde gadsden.verdict: Efficient rookie (9.6 yds/tgt) who held TE1 over Njoku — real upside if the target share climbs.
oronde gadsden.report: Low-volume, strong-efficiency breakout profile: 7.7 ppg on 69 targets with 9.6 yds/tgt and 2.68 pts/touch as a rookie — the exact 'needs only opportunity' quadrant. He sits ahead of veteran Njoku on the depth chart, but that competition is the main risk to volume. Ceiling is a top-8 TE if the Chargers feed him; floor is a boom-bust streamer (stdev 7.4). Take him a round early as a TE upside dart.

greg dulcich.verdict: Athletic, thin room around him — the named late-round dart, but injury tag and 42% snaps temper it.
greg dulcich.report: Small sample (10 gp) but efficient: 15.4% target share, 10.2 yds/tgt, EPA/g 1.95, WOPR 0.30 — low-volume/high-efficiency. Multiple experts call him THE late TE dart given Miami's thin TE competition. Floor is scary: 42% snaps and a Questionable injury tag cap the games-played baseline. Ceiling is a weekly starter if he earns the target funnel. Worth a final-round flier.

cade otton.verdict: 94% snaps and 17.4% share give volume, but 0.21 EPA/g flags efficiency so weak it caps every week.
cade otton.report: High-volume, poor-efficiency quadrant: 94% snaps, WOPR 0.34, 81 targets — yet EPA/g just 0.21 and 1.51 pts/tgt mean the volume produces little. Floor is decent because the role is entrenched with no TB TE threat. Ceiling is limited; he's a bye-week body more than an upside swing. The high stdev (6.0) is noise, not spike weeks. Fine plug, low ceiling.

mike gesicki.verdict: 4.2 ppg crash as snaps fell to 39% behind Erick All — deep aDOT can't offset a shrinking role.
mike gesicki.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency now: target share cratered to 10.3% and snaps to 39% behind a healthy Erick All. The deep aDOT (10.0) gives occasional spike weeks in a great offense, which is the entire ceiling case. Floor is a non-startable role. The 2024 142-point line is stale given the 2025 usage collapse. Purely a bye-week dart.

evan engram.verdict: New Denver, but 1.35 pts/tgt and 42% snaps make this a low-efficiency, age-risk possession piece.
evan engram.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency profile: 6.0 ppg, 1.35 pts/tgt, 6.1 yds/tgt, 42% snaps — Jacksonville already phased him down and he's now in a crowded Denver room. Air-yards share (14.7%) hints at more downfield use if Payton features him, the one ceiling path. Floor is a fringe starter; the two-year efficiency decline is real. Age and role both point down.

david njoku.verdict: Fell to TE2 behind Gadsden after a 5.1 ppg down year — role and efficiency both collapsed.
david njoku.report: Low-volume, negative-efficiency line: 12.5% target share, EPA/g -0.33, and only 11 games — a sharp drop from 2024's 149 points. Now listed behind Oronde Gadsden on a new team, the depth risk is severe. Ceiling exists only if he reclaims the lead role or Gadsden falters. Floor is a non-factor. Draft only as a contingency.

michael mayer.verdict: Stuck behind Brock Bowers with a Questionable tag — talent without a path to volume.
michael mayer.report: Low-volume, negative-efficiency backup: 13.7% target share and WOPR 0.30 came only when Bowers missed time; EPA/g -0.76 is poor. As Vegas's TE2 behind an elite starter, the ceiling requires a Bowers injury. Floor is minimal and the injury tag adds games-missed risk. A pure handcuff to Bowers, not a standalone.

jake tonges.verdict: Kittle's backup with a proj of 33 — only draftable as a leverage handcuff to an injury-prone star.
jake tonges.report: 33% snaps behind George Kittle; the 2.03 pts/tgt and EPA/g 1.42 came in spot duty and shouldn't be read as a full-time projection. Volume is the whole issue — as TE2 he has none while Kittle plays. Ceiling only unlocks on a Kittle injury, when SF's offense would make him a startable TE. Floor is near zero. Stash-only handcuff.

ja'tavion sanders.verdict: Nominal TE1 but 9.2% share and 3.2 ppg say the role is empty — plus a Questionable tag.
ja'tavion sanders.report: Low-volume, poor-efficiency: 9.2% target share, WOPR 0.17, just 8 first downs and 3.2 ppg — barely a fantasy pulse despite being listed TE1. Year-2 leap is the only ceiling case in a young Carolina offense, but the usage gives little to build on. Injury tag and thin production floor make him waiver fodder more than a draft pick.

colby parkinson.verdict: Efficient 2025 (2.32 pts/tgt) but demoted behind rookie Ferguson — role now the killer.
colby parkinson.report: His 7.6 ppg and elite 2.32 pts/tgt came as a starter; now listed TE2 behind rookie Terrance Ferguson, so the volume that drove it is gone. Low-volume/high-efficiency talent with no clear path to snaps. Ceiling requires a Ferguson injury or slow rookie start. Floor is a non-factor. Depth-chart demotion drops him well below the raw stat line.

darnell washington.verdict: Blocking TE trending up (8.5 yds/tgt) but pinned behind Freiermuth — role too small to matter.
darnell washington.report: Efficient on tiny volume: 11.2% target share, 8.5 yds/tgt, EPA/g 1.13 — improving but capped as Pittsburgh's TE2. With Freiermuth's role shrinking, there's a sliver of a path to more receiving work, but the aDOT and usage say blocker first. Floor and ceiling are both low. Speculative only if Freiermuth misses time.

dawson knox.verdict: 6.1 ppg on TD luck (2.12 pts/tgt) as Buffalo's TE2 — efficiency real, volume nonexistent.
dawson knox.report: Low-volume, TD-fueled efficiency: 11% target share and WOPR 0.25 behind Dalton Kincaid, with 2.12 pts/tgt propped by red-zone scores that regress. Buffalo's offense gives touchdown equity, the entire ceiling case. Floor is a non-starter given Kincaid's presence. A pure TD-dependent dart in a good offense.

elijah arroyo.verdict: Loudest player at Seahawks camp — a genuine target-share opening in Year 2 makes him the swing.
elijah arroyo.report: 2025 line is thin (7.9% share, EPA/g -1.25 on 13 games), but the camp signal is concrete: most-discussed Seattle player through 7 practices, 3 TDs in a session, beat writers tying the offense's outlook to his emergence. That's a real opportunity opening ahead of him — the breakout quadrant if the reps convert. He must leapfrog Barner for the receiving role, the chief risk. Take him a round early as a high-variance dart.

eli stowers.verdict: Rookie buried behind Dallas Goedert — no data, no path, deep-stash only.
eli stowers.report: No NFL usage yet and listed as Philadelphia's TE2 behind an established Goedert, so there's no volume to project and the efficiency slate is blank. Ceiling only appears on a Goedert injury in a strong offense; floor is roster-clogging zero. Nothing in the data supports drafting him outside deep dynasty. Watch-list, not a redraft pick.

mason taylor.verdict: Rookie-year 81% snaps and 0.35 WOPR at TE1 volume — genuine ascending sleeper the field ignores
mason taylor.report: High-volume/OK-efficiency quadrant: 17.2% target share, 0.35 WOPR and 81% snaps as a first-year player is real, not TD luck, at only 5.8 aDOT. Ceiling is a low-end TE1 if the Jets pass more and aDOT climbs; floor is the steady 5+ ppg checkdown role he already held over 13 games. Depth-chart label lists Sadiq #1 but the snap data says Taylor is the guy. Start taking him in the last 2-3 rounds as a streaming-plus TE with room to grow.

theo johnson.verdict: Jumped to 7.5 ppg on 17% share and 87% snaps, but the Likely signing is a real ceiling cap
theo johnson.report: High-volume/middling-efficiency: 0.37 WOPR, 8.3 aDOT and 25 first downs show a legit every-down role that nearly doubled his 2024 output. Ceiling is a fringe TE1 if Giants QB play lifts; floor is the same 7 ppg baseline. The listed addition of Isaiah Likely as TE1 is genuine target competition that could shave his snaps and share, so I fade a step. Reasonable late TE flyer, not a bankable starter.

tyler higbee.verdict: Aging TE3 behind rookie Ferguson and Parkinson — volume gone, pure touchdown lottery
tyler higbee.report: Low-volume/decent-efficiency but the efficiency (1.97 pts/tgt) rides tiny sample and TDs; 11% target share, 0.9% air-yards share and 3.3 aDOT is dump-off only. Ceiling requires injuries ahead of him; floor is near-zero fantasy relevance as the third TE. Rams drafted Ferguson and roster Parkinson/Allen, crowding the room. Not draftable outside deep TE-premium formats.

max klare.verdict: Rookie fifth on the Rams TE depth chart with a 10-point projection — undraftable
max klare.report: No NFL data and buried behind Ferguson, Parkinson, Higbee and Allen, so there is nothing to project but hope. Ceiling is minimal unless a cascade of injuries clears the room and the staff prefers him. Floor is zero snaps of fantasy value. This is a name to stash in dynasty, not a redraft asset.

tommy tremble.verdict: Blocking-first TE2 behind Sanders — steady but capped 9% target share
tommy tremble.report: Low-volume/OK-efficiency: 9.1% target share, 0.18 WOPR and 4.4 aDOT define a role-player who has hovered near 3.5 ppg two straight years. Ceiling is a touchdown-fueled 80 if Carolina's passing grows and Sanders slumps; floor is the same low-4 baseline. Ja'Tavion Sanders sits ahead of him and owns the receiving role. Deep-league dart only.

noah gray.verdict: Collapsed to 2.3 ppg with negative receiving EPA behind Kelce — dead weight
noah gray.report: His 2024 6.7 ppg was Kelce-injury inflated; 2025's 8.2% share, 0.16 WOPR and -0.49 rec EPA/g show what he is with Kelce healthy. Ceiling only appears if Kelce misses time, making him a pure handcuff. Floor is the sub-3 ppg reality he just posted over a full season. Not worth a redraft pick unless Kelce news changes.

cole kmet.verdict: Now the TE2 behind rookie Loveland; 9.6% share and cratered output make him a fade
cole kmet.report: Low-volume/decent-efficiency: 0.21 WOPR, 8.8 aDOT and 0.84 rec EPA/g are fine per-touch, but volume fell hard from 2024 as Chicago added Loveland ahead of him. The Smyth 16-PPG-in-complete-games note reflects cherry-picked spike weeks, not the 4.6 ppg full-season reality. Ceiling needs a Loveland injury; floor is the low-relevance role he now occupies. Streamer at best.

noah fant.verdict: 38% snaps and negative EPA behind Juwan Johnson — role shrinking in New Orleans
noah fant.report: Low-volume/fading-efficiency: 9.2% share, 0.16 WOPR, 3.3 aDOT and -0.91 rec EPA/g on just 38% of snaps is a clear downgrade from his 2024 line. Ceiling is a mid-40s TE if the Saints funnel checkdowns his way; floor is irrelevance behind Juwan Johnson. Depth chart and snap trend both point down. Skip in standard leagues.

austin hooper.verdict: Efficient (1.29 EPA/g) but a 7% target-share TE2 behind Pitts — touchdown-dependent
austin hooper.report: Low-volume/strong-efficiency: 9.0 aDOT and elite 1.29 rec EPA/g on only 7.1% target share is the breakout-if-opportunity profile, but Kyle Pitts blocks that opportunity. Ceiling is a low TE2 on red-zone looks; floor is the sub-4 ppg role he just filled. Volume is the ceiling-killer here. Deep-league only unless Pitts moves on.

elijah higgins.verdict: Full-time reps but 6.7% share behind McBride — volume too thin to matter
elijah higgins.report: Low-volume/average-efficiency: 0.12 WOPR and 6.7% target share despite 17 games played means McBride vacuums the passing role. Ceiling is a spot-start week on TD variance; floor is the low-3 ppg he has posted twice. No path to volume with Trey McBride entrenched. Not a draft target.

erick all jr..verdict: Athletic pass-catcher in a great CIN offense, but missed 2025 and stuck behind Gesicki
erick all jr..report: His only sample (2024) was modest and he missed all of 2025, so injury risk is real. In a Burrow-led offense the receiving upside exists if he wins the top TE job, but Mike Gesicki currently sits ahead. Ceiling is a low TE2 if he seizes targets; floor is a lost or backup season. Monitor camp before spending a pick.

will kacmarek.verdict: Undrafted-caliber rookie TE2 in Miami with no data — pure dart throw
will kacmarek.report: No NFL sample and listed behind Greg Dulcich, so projection is guesswork. Ceiling requires him to leapfrog a thin Dolphins TE room and earn targets; floor is inactive weeks. Nothing in the data supports a redraft pick. Watch camp only.

drew sample.verdict: Pure blocking TE — 4.9% share, -0.3 aDOT, zero fantasy pathway
drew sample.report: Low-volume/low-efficiency fade: 0.07 WOPR, -0.3 aDOT and 0.1% air-yards share confirm he is a run-blocker who catches behind the line. Ceiling is a fluke TD week; floor is single-digit season points. Buried behind Gesicki and All on the depth chart. Never draftable.

josh oliver.verdict: Elite per-touch (3.67 pts/touch) but a 6.5% share blocking role behind Hockenson
josh oliver.report: Low-volume/strong-efficiency: 2.89 pts/tgt and 0.88 rec EPA/g are excellent, but 0.12 WOPR and 46% snaps as a blocker cap the ceiling hard. Best case is a handful of TD spikes; floor is the low-3 ppg role beneath T.J. Hockenson. Great efficiency without volume equals a non-starter. Fade in standard formats.

eli raridon.verdict: Rookie behind Hunter Henry with no NFL data — deep dynasty stash, not redraft
eli raridon.report: No sample and sits behind entrenched Hunter Henry, so there is no volume path in 2026. Ceiling is minimal barring injury ahead of him; floor is inactive or blocking-only. Nothing here supports a redraft selection. Camp watch only.

charlie kolar.verdict: TE3 on the Chargers behind Gadsden and Njoku — efficient scraps, no volume
charlie kolar.report: Low-volume/strong-efficiency: 2.41 pts/tgt and 9.5 yds/tgt look nice but on a 4.6% target share and 0.09 WOPR it is noise. Ceiling is an occasional TD week; floor is total irrelevance third on the chart. Gadsden and Njoku own the room. Not draftable.

mitchell evans.verdict: Second-year TE3 in a crowded Carolina room — 6.4% share caps everything
mitchell evans.report: Low-volume/average-efficiency: 0.12 WOPR, 3.6 aDOT and 37% snaps put him behind Sanders and Tremble. Ceiling needs multiple injuries ahead; floor is the sub-3 ppg role he showed as a rookie. No clear path to targets. Deep-dynasty name only.

cade stover.verdict: HOU TE3 behind Schultz with 1.2 ppg and negative EPA — no fantasy case
cade stover.report: Low-volume/low-efficiency fade: 1.9 aDOT, -0.71 rush EPA/g and 1.24 pts/touch over a fractured season signal a bottom-of-roster role. Ceiling is a garbage-time TD; floor is inactive weeks behind Dalton Schultz. Nothing to draft here.

john bates.verdict: Blocking TE listed Questionable, behind Okonkwo — near-zero receiving role
john bates.report: Low-volume/low-efficiency: 6.8% share, 3.0 aDOT and 51% snaps in a run-block role, plus a Questionable tag. Ceiling is a rare red-zone score; floor is single-digit points and missed time. Chig Okonkwo owns the passing role in Washington. Undraftable.

tanner hudson.verdict: Fifth on the Bengals TE chart at 15% snaps — noise, not a fantasy option
tanner hudson.report: Low-volume/OK-efficiency but on 15% snaps and a 6.4% target share it is meaningless; 0.12 WOPR and TE5 depth cap any upside. Ceiling requires an implausible injury cascade; floor is inactive. Gesicki, All and Sample all rank ahead. Never draft.

adam trautman.verdict: Blocking TE2 behind Engram with a 4.8% target share; touchdown-or-bust roster filler
adam trautman.report: Low-volume, low-air-yards profile (WOPR 0.10, aDOT 4.6): high-volume/poor-quadrant is not even reached — he's low-volume with modest efficiency (1.98 pts/tgt). Two straight years near 2.6-2.7 PPG confirm a stable non-fantasy role behind Evan Engram. Ceiling requires an Engram injury; floor is basically what he already is. Only worth a late dart in deepest TE-premium formats.

luke schoonmaker.verdict: Buried TE3 behind Ferguson; production halved in 2025, no path to volume
luke schoonmaker.report: Low-volume/low-efficiency fade quadrant: 33% snap share, 4.6% target share and 1.18 pts/tgt in 2025, down from a modest 2024. Jake Ferguson locks the passing-down role, with Trigg added ahead of him. Ceiling needs a Ferguson injury and even then the offense funnels elsewhere. Floor is near-zero fantasy relevance; not draftable outside 20-team leagues.

jackson hawes.verdict: Efficient rookie blocker (2.77 pts/tgt, 1.14 EPA/g) but stuck at TE3 behind Kincaid/Knox
jackson hawes.report: Strong per-touch efficiency on tiny volume — the low-volume/strong-efficiency breakout quadrant, but the depth chart caps opportunity behind Dalton Kincaid and Dawson Knox. WOPR 0.12 and 44% snaps mean the role is real but limited. Ceiling opens only with an injury ahead; floor is a red-zone-dependent 3 PPG. Efficiency is intriguing enough to monitor, not to draft.

mo alie-cox.verdict: Aging TE3 behind rookie stud Tyler Warren; negative EPA seals the fade
mo alie-cox.report: Low-volume/poor-efficiency fade: -0.08 rec EPA/g, 4.7 aDOT, just 4 first downs across 11 games. Tyler Warren commands the position and Alie-Cox is a blocking body at age-33 territory. Two years of sub-2 PPG confirm no fantasy role. Neither floor nor ceiling justifies a pick; pure depth flyer.

daniel bellinger.verdict: Best deep-TE bet here: 1.74 EPA/g, 9.4 aDOT, real 2025 role in Tennessee
daniel bellinger.report: A genuine step forward in 2025 — 60 pts, 6.3% target share, WOPR 0.14 and downfield usage (aDOT 9.4) with the best EPA in this tier. That's the low-volume/strong-efficiency quadrant with room to grow if Gunnar Helm doesn't seize the job. Ceiling is a matchup-based streamer; high stdev (4.9) reflects TD-dependence. Floor is the 2024 disappearing act. Worth a last-round stash.

ben sinnott.verdict: Efficient on 13 targets but TE3 behind Okonkwo; needs a role that isn't there
ben sinnott.report: Tiny sample shows decent efficiency (2.18 pts/tgt, WOPR 0.15) — low-volume/good-efficiency, the breakout archetype, but Chig Okonkwo and John Bates sit ahead and he played only 9 games. Ceiling requires injuries and a leap in snap share above 36%. Floor is irrelevance. A dynasty-flavored dart, not a redraft asset.

jeremy ruckert.verdict: Checkdown TE (3.5 aDOT) buried behind rookie Sadiq and Mason Taylor
jeremy ruckert.report: Improved to 7.3% target share but the 3.5 aDOT and 2.9% air-yards share scream dump-off role with no ceiling — high targets, poor efficiency per opportunity. The Jets loaded up with Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor ahead of him, shrinking his path. Ceiling is a bye-week plug; floor is off the fantasy map. Skip in redraft.

luke musgrave.verdict: On PUP behind Tucker Kraft; upside real but availability and depth both against him
luke musgrave.report: When active in 2025 he flashed the best volume in this group (WOPR 0.18, 8.5% targets, 8.6 aDOT) — low-volume/decent-efficiency with breakout genes. But Tucker Kraft is entrenched and Musgrave opens on PUP, capping games and snaps. Ceiling needs a Kraft injury plus health; floor is a redshirt-type season. High-variance stash only.

durham smythe.verdict: Blocking specialist behind Mark Andrews; zero fantasy pulse
durham smythe.report: Lowest-of-low quadrant: 2.9% target share, 0.9% air-yards, WOPR 0.05, -0.04 EPA and 1 first down in 7 games. Mark Andrews owns every target that matters in Baltimore. Ceiling is a spot TD; floor is nothing. Undraftable in any standard format.

davis allen.verdict: Productive 2025 fill-in now TE4 in a crowded Rams room and dinged
davis allen.report: 63 pts and 2.62 pts/touch in 2025 came on genuine snaps (50%), but the Rams reshuffled to Terrance Ferguson, Parkinson and Higbee, dropping Allen to TE4 while listed questionable. Efficiency was fine on a low aDOT (3.9) checkdown role. Ceiling requires injuries clearing the path; floor is inactive weeks. Wait-and-see, not a draft pick.

foster moreau.verdict: 2024's 103-pt line is dead weight; 2025 collapse and TE4 role in Houston
foster moreau.report: The 2024 breakout (6.1 PPG, 2.40 pts/tgt) reversed hard in 2025: 0.8 PPG, aDOT 1.0, -0.53 EPA over 7 games. Now behind Dalton Schultz and buried at TE4. Do not project the old season forward — the recent usage says the role is gone. Ceiling is a desperation stream; floor is zero. Fade.

nate adkins.verdict: Third Denver TE behind Engram and Trautman; no viable target path
nate adkins.report: Efficiency cratered from 2024 (2.90 pts/tgt) to 2025 (1.53, -0.10 EPA) as his role shrank to 33% snaps over 9 games. Buried behind Engram and Trautman on the same depth chart. Low volume, weak efficiency — a fade. Ceiling is a TD spike; floor is irrelevance.

brock wright.verdict: LaPorta's blocking backup; 8.8% targets are all at the line (1.0 aDOT)
brock wright.report: The 8.8% target share looks like volume until you see aDOT 1.0, 1.3% air-yards and -0.24 EPA — dump-offs, the high-usage/poor-efficiency warning that the touches carry no fantasy value. Sam LaPorta owns the real role. Ceiling is TD-driven variance (stdev 3.5); floor is a couple points a week. Not draftable.

nate boerkircher.verdict: Undrafted-profile rookie TE2 behind Brenton Strange; pure dart with no data
nate boerkircher.report: No NFL production to interpret and slotted behind Brenton Strange in Jacksonville. As an unproven rookie with no advanced usage, there's nothing to project forward beyond depth-chart position. Ceiling is a camp surprise; floor is the practice squad. Dynasty-only name to file away.

payne durham.verdict: Fourth Buccaneer TE behind Otton; 1.7% target share says invisible
payne durham.report: Efficient in a 2024 cameo (2.46 pts/tgt) but 2025 usage was near-nil — 1.7% target share, WOPR 0.03, 1 first down. Cade Otton is the entrenched starter and Durham sits at TE4. No volume, no path. Ceiling is a garbage-time TD; floor is inactive. Fade.

joe royer.verdict: Rookie TE2 behind breakout Harold Fannin; no data, no role
joe royer.report: No collegiate-to-NFL data provided and buried behind Harold Fannin in Cleveland's TE room. With nothing to project and QB uncertainty in the offense, there's no case for fantasy relevance. Ceiling is emergency snaps; floor is nonexistence. Skip.

ben sims.verdict: Tiny 3-game sample flashed downfield role (aDOT 12.2, WOPR 0.22) but TE3 in Miami
ben sims.report: The lone intriguing sliver: 12.2 aDOT, 13.5% air-yards share and WOPR 0.22 across 3 games hint at a real receiving profile — low-volume/strong-efficiency — but 13% overall snaps and a spot behind Dulcich cap it hard. Ceiling needs the depth chart to collapse; floor is a healthy scratch. Monitor camp, don't draft.

luke farrell.verdict: Kittle's blocking backup in SF; 3.2% targets and lowest projection in the tier
luke farrell.report: Low-volume/low-value profile: 3.2% target share, WOPR 0.06, aDOT 2.9 — a run-blocking role with no fantasy pathway behind George Kittle. Efficiency ticked up in 2025 but on negligible touches. Ceiling is a fluke TD week; floor is zero. The 10-point projection is honest. Undraftable.

josh allen.verdict: Elite dual-threat workhorse with unmatched floor; 112 carries and QB1-caliber passing make him the safe QB1.
josh allen.report: High volume, high efficiency — the safe expensive quadrant. Two straight 365+ seasons at 92% snaps with 100+ carries and elite rush/pass EPA; the rushing floor immunizes him from TD regression. Ceiling is another overall QB1 (410+); floor is still top-five (~320) given durability. No depth competition. Only real cost is the early-3rd draft price for a position you can wait on, but nothing in the data argues against it.

jayden daniels.verdict: Elite rushing volume and a 20.9 PPG rookie year; the 2025 injury, not talent, is the only knock.
jayden daniels.report: High volume when healthy — 148 carries in 2024 drove a top-five finish; 2025's 6.7 PPG is a 7-game injury artifact, not decline. The ceiling is a top-three dual-threat season with McLaurin and now Diggs, plus a soft-defense/high-pass-volume script in Washington. Floor is scary (~235) because the rushing style carries real injury risk, already realized once. Undisputed starter. Bet on the profile.

lamar jackson.verdict: 2024 was a historic 430-point ceiling; rushing-TD decline and 2025 injury pull the range wide.
lamar jackson.report: High volume, elite efficiency in 2024 (25.3 PPG); 2025's 12.6 PPG reflects only 13 games and softer play. The ceiling is again the overall QB1, but rushing TDs have fallen since Henry's arrival — he no longer runs inside the 5, capping the rushing-TD edge that made him unbeatable. Floor (~250) is a missed-games risk. Still one of the highest-upside QBs; just priced near that ceiling.

drake maye.verdict: League-best efficiency (CPOE 12.2, EPA 9.72) and rising volume; lowest-variance breakout at QB.
drake maye.report: Broke out in 2025 to 20.7 PPG with the NFL's top passing efficiency and a tiny 5.2 weekly stdev — the safest weekly profile here. Weapons upgraded (AJ Brown, Doubs) and a harder schedule means more close games and 4th-quarter snaps he sat out in 2025 blowouts. Only 20% of points came from rushing, so he isn't rush-dependent. Ceiling is a top-three finish (~375); floor (~285) is elevated by that consistency. Clear-cut starter.

jalen hurts.verdict: Tush-push rushing TDs anchor a solid floor, but the offense's 2025 slide and brutal playoff slate cap upside.
jalen hurts.report: High rushing volume (105-150 carries) and goal-line role keep him TD-rich, but 2025 pass efficiency (EPA 2.14) reflects an offense that fell to ~19th in scoring. New OC Kellen Mond is a swing factor either way. Ceiling ~350 if the passing rebounds; floor ~265 on the rushing baseline. The killer is fantasy playoffs — SEA wk15 and HOU wk16 are his two hardest matchups back-to-back. Locked-in starter.

joe burrow.verdict: Elite pocket passer with a passing-only QB1 ceiling; 2025 was injury, not decline — health is the bet.
