joe burrow.report: Efficient, high-volume passer (21.9 PPG in 2024, EPA 4.58 in his 8 healthy 2025 games) in an offense that throws in every script, especially near the goal line. Ceiling is a top-three passing season (~385) with Chase and Higgins; floor (~235) is entirely a games-played question after a lost 2025. Almost no rushing, so it's a pure volume/efficiency profile. Soft playoff slate (CAR, IND) is a plus. Bet on health.

jaxson dart.verdict: Rushing-driven year-two breakout, but Matt Nagy and a halved designed-run rate cloud the ceiling.
jaxson dart.report: Strong rush EPA (2.72) and 4.9 yards before contact show real rushing upside, but designed carries were roughly cut in half after Daboll left and after multiple concussion checks — the exact volume the ceiling depends on. All his worst games came vs top-five defenses he faced often. ESPN's sleeper call fits, but at ADP 75 (inside the top 100) he isn't a late-round steal, so no sleeper badge. Ceiling ~330 if the rushing holds; floor ~215 if Nagy tames it.

trevor lawrence.verdict: Second-half QB1 run and real goal-line rushing volume make him a quality streamer at a light price.
trevor lawrence.report: Full-time (97% snaps) with efficient passing and a sustainable rushing-TD profile — third-most carries from the 1-yard line, nine TDs on eight expected. Second-half 2025 he was the overall QB1 (22.8 PPG). Ceiling ~330 given the volume and easing schedule; floor ~235. His analyst rank (QB9) sits well ahead of a QB11-ish ADP, and the usage backs the cheaper cost. Playoff wart: @HOU wk15, where he scored 8 last year. Firm starter.

dak prescott.verdict: Consistent QB7-8 passing production with strong weapons, but no rushing caps the ceiling.
dak prescott.report: High-volume, efficient passer (EPA 6.66, 18.5 PPG) with good receivers, line and coaching — a reliable value starter. Ceiling (~320) is limited because he no longer runs (53 carries, negative rush EPA); floor (~245) is steady. A likely-improved defense could add pass volume in shootouts. This is a floor-over-ceiling profile you take late as a set-and-forget QB2, not a difference-maker. Clear starter.

bo nix.verdict: Rising dropback volume, elite line and a Waddle addition make him a cheap high-floor QB2.
bo nix.report: Full 100% snap share with a stable ~18 PPG across two years — the same profile that once cost a QB7-8 pick, now half price. Efficiency is average (CPOE -1.1) but volume, an excellent offensive line and Jaylen Waddle support the ceiling (~330). Some rushing (83 carries) adds a modest floor (~250). Not a league-winner, but a strong value if you wait at QB. Undisputed starter.

brock purdy.verdict: Elite Shanahan-system efficiency with QB1-line volume when healthy; ADP outside 100 is a clear value.
brock purdy.report: Low-volume 2025 sample (9 games) but ridiculous efficiency — EPA 7.01, CPOE 7.7, plus underrated rushing (~4 pts/game on the ground). He was QB2 in PPG through wk17 before a brutal playoff slate tanked the season line. At ADP 104 the opportunity/efficiency edge clearly beats the price — start taking him around round 9 as your QB. Floor ~220 (injury/tough SF playoff slate: @KC, PHI); ceiling ~330. Firm starter.

matthew stafford.verdict: Led the NFL in passing TDs — regression is near-certain and there's zero rushing to backstop it.
matthew stafford.report: High passing volume and efficiency (EPA 8.85) drove a 20.6-PPG 2025, but that was fueled by a league-leading TD rate that almost certainly regresses. With literally no rushing (negative rush EPA), there's no floor beneath the passing, so the range narrows down (floor ~240, ceiling ~320). Better as a superflex piece than a 1QB target; don't pay for a repeat top-four finish. Starter, but age/decline-adjacent.

caleb williams.verdict: Year-two leap under Ben Johnson with rushing and end-zone volume; a cheap high-ceiling QB2.
caleb williams.report: Improving dual-threat — 18.7 PPG with 77 carries and third-most end-zone attempts in the NFL; second-half 2025 (~20.6 PPG) showed the Ben Johnson system clicking with turnovers/sacks down. Passing efficiency still developing (CPOE -3.4), which caps but doesn't kill the ceiling (~340). Rushing gives a solid floor (~250). Loveland and Burden add upside. At ADP 92 a fine value, though just inside the top 100 so no sleeper tag. Starter.

justin herbert.verdict: McDaniel-system fit, healthy line and a dream playoff slate make him a sneaky-value QB at ADP 109.
justin herbert.report: Steady mid-QB1 volume (16.9 PPG, 83 carries) with modest efficiency; the upside case is a new McDaniel offense that historically maximizes accurate clean-pocket passers, plus red-zone rushing. Easy fantasy playoffs (SF, @MIA, KC — no elite defense, no weather) raise the win-your-league ceiling (~330). At an ADP outside the top 100, start taking him around round 9-10 as a high-floor QB with schedule-driven upside. Floor ~240. Firm starter.

patrick mahomes.verdict: Coming off ACL with passing points already at bust-year levels; a name-tax risk, not a value.
patrick mahomes.report: Much of 2025's 16.8 PPG came from scrambling (2.08 rush EPA, 6.6 ypc) — exactly what an ACL recovery threatens. Passing fantasy points are already near his floor, and Rice's return may cost him rushing yardage. Expect a more run-heavy KC offense with Kenneth Walker. Ceiling remains ~335 on talent, but floor (~230) and the injury tag make ADP 106 fair, not cheap. Health is listed Questionable — monitor. Starter when healthy.

kyler murray.verdict: New team, unsettled QB battle — but if he wins it, rushing upside in a loaded MIN offense is a real value.
kyler murray.report: Camp notes have him leading the McCarthy competition on reps as of Aug 5, but it's unsettled — that's the swing. 2024's 17.5 PPG with 78 carries shows the rushing floor, and this system produced QB6/QB9 for less mobile passers; now with Jefferson, Addison and Jennings the ceiling is a top-10 finish (~305). Floor collapses (~130) if he loses the job. At ADP 150, worth the dart in round 12+ once the starter is confirmed. Watch for the announcement.

tyler shough.verdict: Now the undisputed NO starter after a strong finish; fast-pace offense makes him a cheap streamer sleeper.
tyler shough.report: The FantasyPros/ESPN sleeper call holds up: QB12 in PPG from Week 9 with six straight 17+ games to close, and he's now the clear starter. Efficiency is unspectacular (CPOE -2.7) but volume and pace, plus some designed runs, support a QB2-with-upside profile. Ceiling ~290 if the passing volume and rushing stick; floor ~180 given the thin efficiency. At ADP 154 he's a round-13 streamer worth the shot. Named starter.

jared goff.verdict: Consistent, efficient passer but zero rushing and a career-best QB7 cap him as a value starter, not a winner.
jared goff.report: High-volume, efficient in Detroit's offense (EPA 6.26, 17.5 PPG, tiny 7.3 stdev), but literally no rushing (19 carries, negative rush EPA) puts a hard ceiling near his career-best QB7 (~305). Floor is reliable (~235) thanks to the offense and consistency. This is a fine late-round 1QB plug or superflex piece, not an upside swing. Locked-in starter.

daniel jones.verdict: QB1 in a top offense last year with 25% rushing points; cheap at ADP 160 despite Achilles risk.
daniel jones.report: Efficient (EPA 5.02) and rushing-driven (45 carries, positive rush EPA) as the starter of a top-scoring Indianapolis offense — a genuine value at ADP 160. The Achilles recovery threatens the rushing share the ceiling leans on, and Richardson/Leonard lurk. Ceiling ~290 if healthy and the volume holds; floor ~175 given injury and depth risk. Start taking him in the last rounds as an upside QB2. Nominal starter — monitor health.

baker mayfield.verdict: 2024's 21.5-PPG form under Coen is the bet; 2025 injury-suppressed line makes ADP 149 a value swing.
baker mayfield.report: 2024 was a legit QB-good season (21.5 PPG); 2025's dip to 16.0 came with injuries dragging even his complete games. Efficiency metrics are middling (EPA 0.04, CPOE -2.5), but 55 carries and 7 broken tackles add a rushing kicker, and a soft playoff slate (NO, @ATL, LAR) helps. Ceiling ~310 on a healthy bounce-back; floor ~210. At ADP 149 it's a late-round upside bet on 2024 repeating. Firm starter.

malik willis.verdict: Rushing-only late swing now atop Miami's QB room; ceiling is real if he runs, floor is a benching for Ewers.
malik willis.report: Willis is a low passing-volume, high-rush-efficiency profile: 22 carries at 5.6 ypc in limited 2025 work and elite small-sample pass EPA (7.02/g) that won't hold, but the rushing floor is the bet. With Tua gone he's QB1, and 8 designed-run points a week is a genuine top-12 path if the job holds. Floor is Quinn Ewers taking over. Sleeper: opportunity just opened for a runner — start taking him around Round 13.

jordan love.verdict: Highest floor of this tier on 94% snaps and positive EPA, but TD regression and weather cap the ceiling.
jordan love.report: Love is the safe high-volume passer here: two straight 13.8-ppg seasons, 94% snap share, +7.4 pass EPA/g, and modest legs (47 carries). Ceiling is a low-end QB1 if the passing TDs and a Jacobs-fueled offense click. Floor is stable given the full-time role. The knock is negative TD regression risk and three cold-weather fantasy playoff games (MIA, @CHI, HOU). Solid streaming anchor, not an upside play.

cam ward.verdict: Year-two leap candidate; rookie EPA was ugly but the full-time role and legs give a QB1 outcome band.
cam ward.report: Ward posted an alarming -6.42 pass EPA/g as a rookie but played all 17 at 95% snaps and added rushing value (3 broken tackles, 1.6 YAC/rush). He's the classic low-efficiency, high-volume profile whose year-two improvement is the whole thesis. Ceiling is a Goff/Lawrence-style QB11 jump; floor is the rookie inefficiency lingering behind a rebuilding line. Weapons around him are improving. A cheap breakout dart.

c.j. stroud.verdict: Talented, high-volume passer who simply won't run — that caps a QB whose defense often kills game scripts.
c.j. stroud.report: Stroud is a solid-volume passer (91% snaps, 48 carries but negligible designed-run value) with only average per-dropback output the last two years (12-13 ppg). The ceiling requires a passing-TD spike since he offers almost no rushing points and drifts to throw rather than scramble. Floor is fine given the locked role and added Montgomery run game. Playoff slate (JAX, @PHI, @GB) is a mixed bag. Fine QB2, limited league-winner odds.

sam darnold.verdict: Best 2024 season in this tier (18.1 ppg) plus strong CPOE; Seattle context is the swing factor.
sam darnold.report: Darnold pairs full-time volume (96% snaps) with genuinely good accuracy metrics (CPOE 6.2), and his 2024 18.1-ppg outlier shows the ceiling when the situation is right. He offers essentially no rushing (2.7 ypc, -0.76 rush EPA), so it's a pure passing bet. Ceiling is a repeat top-10; floor is the mediocre 2025 (13.8 ppg) with fewer designed runs. Efficient-per-dropback profile makes him a strong late QB target.

bryce young.verdict: Quietly improving with real rushing volume (54 carries); still low passing efficiency limits the ceiling.
bryce young.report: Young trended up in 2025 (12.8 ppg, +2 broken tackles, 54 carries) but his pass EPA stayed slightly negative (-1.37), a high-volume/low-efficiency line that keeps him a streamer. The rushing adds a floor most in this range lack, and continued development is the ceiling case at 97% snaps. Floor is the erratic passer from 2024 (10.2 stdev). Reasonable dart in the final QB rounds.

fernando mendoza.verdict: Rookie starter with no pro data and a shaky Vegas supporting cast; pure projection dart.
fernando mendoza.report: Mendoza opens as Vegas' QB1 with Cousins and O'Connell behind him, but there's zero NFL usage or efficiency to grade — the ESPN 187 projection is a guess. Ceiling depends on rushing ability translating and the offense supporting a rookie; floor is a rookie benching or a bad line dragging his output down. No advanced numbers to lean on, so I'm inferring risk from the profile. Wait-and-see only.

geno smith.verdict: New team and better weapons revive interest, but 2025's collapse and age argue for restraint.
geno smith.report: Smith cratered in 2025 (10.2 ppg, -4.86 pass EPA) after a strong 2024 (15.6 ppg, 5.1 ypc), a big decline for a 13-year vet. The RotoWire call cites a better line and pass catchers in the new spot, which is a legit context upgrade, but I'm skeptical the arm and legs bounce all the way back — hence I'm holding off the sleeper tag. Ceiling is a return toward 2024; floor is more 2025. Streamer at best.

aaron rodgers.verdict: Steady late-career passer for now, but zero rushing and age make this a fading, low-ceiling profile.
aaron rodgers.report: Rodgers still posted 13.4 ppg on 96% snaps in 2025 with a modest +1.68 pass EPA, so the floor as a full-time starter is playable. But he offers no rushing value (0.1 YAC/rush) and the trend is down from 15.1 ppg in 2024 at age 42. Ceiling is a low-end QB1 week-to-week; the real risk is a mid-season decline or benching for Rudolph. Pittsburgh playoff slate (BAL, CAR, @TEN) is average. Streamer only.

jacoby brissett.verdict: Pure volume play — Arizona's ~50 dropbacks/game can float weekly QB1 lines despite poor efficiency.
jacoby brissett.report: Brissett is the textbook high-volume/low-efficiency QB: 25th in points per dropback yet a weekly QB1 in 2025 (13.4 ppg) because Arizona throws constantly. With Kyler elsewhere he holds the job, and that raw pass volume plus some rushing (0.53 rush EPA, 2 broken tackles) is the whole edge. Floor is the mediocre efficiency catching up; ceiling is another volume-carried QB1 stretch. Sleeper on volume alone — start considering in Round 15.

deshaun watson.verdict: Unsettled starter competing with Sanders and coming off dreadful play; not draftable in redraft.
deshaun watson.report: Watson's last real data (4.5 ppg in 2024) was catastrophic, and camp reports frame an open competition with Shedeur Sanders. Projection of 124 signals ESPN expects a partial or losing role. Ceiling requires winning the job AND rediscovering pre-injury form, a long shot; floor is a backup by midseason. No usage edge to bank on. Avoid.

tua tagovailoa.verdict: New team, questionable tag, and a Penix competition — a low, injury-fragile projection with no rushing.
tua tagovailoa.report: Tua brings a full-time snap history (95%) but weak fantasy output (9.5 ppg 2025) and zero rushing (-0.53 rush EPA), and he's tagged Questionable with Penix behind him in Atlanta. The 115 projection screams partial season. Ceiling is a healthy, efficient passing stretch; floor is another injury absence or a benching. Too much uncertainty to roster in single-QB.

shedeur sanders.verdict: Rookie stuck in a two-QB fight behind Watson; poor 2025 efficiency, but the legs flashed.
shedeur sanders.report: Sanders' 2025 line was rough (5.0 ppg, -7.41 pass EPA, -6.6 CPOE) though he showed real rushing juice (5.5 YBC/rush, 2.6 YAC). He's listed QB2 behind Watson with an open competition per camp reports. Ceiling is winning the job and running enough to matter; floor is clipboard duty. The passing efficiency is a genuine red flag. Speculative only.

kirk cousins.verdict: Backup behind Mendoza with dead legs; only an injury opens the door — not rosterable.
kirk cousins.report: Cousins is Vegas' QB2 with a 46-point projection, and his usage shows why: no rushing (0.5 ypc, essentially 0 YBC) and declining passing (6.1 ppg, -4.5 CPOE in 2025). The only path to value is a Mendoza injury, at which point he'd be a low-ceiling pocket passer. Floor is inactive. Waiver-wire contingency at most.

michael penix jr..verdict: Buried behind Tua with murky depth status; talent flickers but the role isn't there yet.
michael penix jr..report: Penix showed a slight positive pass EPA (0.57) and some rushing value (0.79 rush EPA) in 2025 but only 7.1 ppg and now sits behind a healthy-ish Tua in Atlanta. His path is entirely job-dependent — a Tua injury (Questionable) is the realistic opening. Ceiling is a mid-range starter run; floor is a season of holding the clipboard. Stash-only.

j.j. mccarthy.verdict: Now the backup behind Kyler in Minnesota; 40-point projection means bench-only value.
j.j. mccarthy.report: McCarthy flashed mobility in his 2025 sample (37 carries, 5 broken tackles, 4.9 ypc) but the passing was poor (-5.41 pass EPA, -4.8 CPOE) and he's projected as QB2 behind Murray. Only an injury unlocks his dual-threat ceiling. Floor is inactive most weeks. Not a redraft asset in single-QB formats.

carson beck.verdict: Rookie QB2 in Arizona with no NFL data; pure contingency stash, undraftable in redraft.
carson beck.report: Beck has zero pro usage and projects at 29 points as Brissett's backup. There's nothing to grade beyond depth-chart position, and the path to relevance is an injury to a starter Arizona clearly prefers. Ceiling is a spot-start stretch; floor is inactive all year. Skip.

justin fields.verdict: Backup to Mahomes; elite rushing makes him a lottery ticket only if the starter goes down.
justin fields.report: Fields carries genuine rushing upside (71 carries, 5.4 ypc, 3 broken tackles, 0.97 rush EPA) that would make him startable if he ever played — but he's stuck behind Mahomes with an 11-point projection. His passing is the problem (-6.9 CPOE). The only realistic value is an injury unlock, where his legs give a high weekly ceiling. Floor is inactive. Deep contingency.

joe flacco.verdict: Aging backup behind Burrow; no path to volume, no rushing — not a redraft consideration.
joe flacco.report: Flacco is Cincinnati's QB2 with an 11-point projection. His 2025 line as a fill-in (8.6 ppg, -3.14 pass EPA) and non-existent legs cap any spot-start value, and he only plays if Burrow misses time. Ceiling is a short low-efficiency starting run; floor is inactive. Avoid.

mac jones.verdict: 49ers backup with a decent efficiency flash, but Purdy blocks all volume — undraftable.
mac jones.report: Jones actually posted a respectable +4.06 pass EPA and +4.0 CPOE in 2025 relief work, the profile of a competent fill-in, but he sits behind Purdy at 74% career snap ceiling and a 9-point projection. Value requires a Purdy injury; even then he offers no rushing. Floor is inactive; ceiling is a caretaker stint. Streamer contingency only.

jameis winston.verdict: Aging QB2 buried behind rookie Jaxson Dart; only startable if Dart goes down — undraftable in 1QB.
jameis winston.report: Winston is the clear #2 on NYG behind Jaxson Dart, so 2025's minimal snaps (68% over just 3g, ugly -12.1 CPOE) reflect mop-up duty. His 2024 line (7.7 ppg, 131 pts) shows he can produce gunslinger-volume points if pressed into starting, and he's a proven high-variance passer. Floor is the bench — he only has value if Dart is injured. Low-volume, poor-efficiency profile; leave him on the wire until an injury creates a path.

ty simpson.verdict: Rookie clipboard-holder behind Stafford; zero data and no clear path — a name to stash, not draft.
ty simpson.report: Simpson has no NFL usage to grade, so any projection is pure speculation on a rookie behind entrenched starter Matthew Stafford. The only real case is Stafford's age and durability risk cracking the door, but that's a bet on injury, not opportunity currently in hand. Camp intel is generic and settles nothing about his role. No volume, no efficiency baseline — this is a deep dynasty stash, not a 2026 redraft asset.

anthony richardson sr..verdict: Proven rushing-QB ceiling but ESPN projects zero — buried on the depth chart with no clear 2026 role.
anthony richardson sr..report: Richardson's 2024 (9.6 ppg, 86 carries, 5.8 ypc) shows real designed-run upside that gives any starting QB a fantasy floor from legs alone. But the 2026 projection of 0 and murky depth chart signal he's not expected to play, so that rushing profile is locked in a cage. His passing has always been the problem, not the volume. If he wins a job anywhere his rushing makes him a QB1 streamer, but that's a big if — waiver watch only.

jarrett stidham.verdict: Solidly behind Bo Nix with no path; a single mop-up snap in 2025 tells the whole story.
jarrett stidham.report: Stidham is the #2 in Denver behind an established Bo Nix, and his 2025 sample is a lone 6%-snap appearance. There's no volume, no efficiency signal, and no realistic route to starting barring injury. He's a veteran caretaker, not a fantasy asset in any single-QB format. Nothing here to draft.

nick mullens.verdict: Career backup behind Trevor Lawrence; a nice CPOE blip on 11% snaps means nothing for volume.
nick mullens.report: Mullens flashed a strong 26.2 CPOE in 2025, but that's on tiny relief-duty volume (11% snaps over 5g) and can't be projected forward as a starter's role. He sits firmly behind Trevor Lawrence with no path to snaps. Low-volume, decent-efficiency, but the volume simply isn't coming. Undraftable in 1QB leagues.

jake browning.verdict: Backup behind Baker Mayfield with a brutal -7.68 pass EPA/g sample — no path and no efficiency.
jake browning.report: Browning's 2025 relief work was poor: -7.68 pass EPA/g on 73% snaps over 5 games, just 2.9 ppg. He's clearly behind Baker Mayfield in Tampa with no starting path. The combination of no volume and genuinely bad per-snap production makes this a fade even if injury struck. Nothing to see here for redraft.

tommy devito.verdict: Third-string-caliber backup behind Drake Maye; 2024's 0.8 ppg shows no fantasy pulse.
tommy devito.report: DeVito sits behind ascending starter Drake Maye and offers essentially no fantasy production history (0.8 ppg in 2024 spot duty). No meaningful volume, no efficiency edge, and no injury-independent path to relevance. He's a roster body, not a draftable QB in any standard format.

marcus mariota.verdict: Best of these backups: proven rushing floor if Jayden Daniels misses time, but only as an injury dart.
marcus mariota.report: Mariota is the most useful arm here — 2025 gave 7.4 ppg with 50 carries and legit rushing (5.3 yds before contact/rush), so if Jayden Daniels misses time he becomes an instant streamer with a dual-threat floor. The catch: Daniels is a durable, elite starter, so Mariota's snaps are capped at garbage time. Modest volume with real mobility, but no standalone path. Handcuff-tier only — grab off waivers if Daniels is dinged.

tyson bagent.verdict: Backup behind Caleb Williams; a small-sample CPOE spike doesn't create a role that doesn't exist.
tyson bagent.report: Bagent posted a shiny 19.7 CPOE on 7% snaps in 2025, but that's noise on a two-game sample, not a projectable trend. He's firmly behind Caleb Williams with no starting path. Low volume, no reliable efficiency signal at scale — nothing to draft in single-QB leagues.

sam howell.verdict: QB3 in Dallas behind Dak and Milton — two injuries deep, effectively undraftable.
sam howell.report: Howell is listed as the #3 in Dallas behind Dak Prescott and Joe Milton, so he'd need two players ahead of him to fall before seeing snaps. No 2025 usage and no realistic path make him irrelevant for 2026 redraft. His prior Washington starting stretch showed streamer-level upside at best if ever pressed in. Pure roster filler.

jakobi meyers.verdict: Safe PPR floor on high slot volume in JAX, but modest efficiency and TD scarcity cap the ceiling.
jakobi meyers.report: High-volume slot in JAX: 22.9% target share, WOPR 0.54, 85% snaps — a safe PPR floor from consistent short-area work (stdev 4.8). Efficiency is modest (7.6 yds/tgt, 1.6 YAC), so this is high-volume/moderate-efficiency: dependable but capped. New team behind Brian Thomas limits target ceiling and TDs are scarce. The floor is the draw at this cost.

wan'dale robinson.verdict: Elite reception volume makes him PPR-safe, though the TEN move threatens his monster target share.
wan'dale robinson.report: Elite 2025 volume — 30.3% target share, WOPR 0.65, 91% snaps, 92 catches — high-volume/good-efficiency slot (rec EPA 1.22) that's PPR gold. But that share predates the TEN move; Carnell Tate and Ridley now compete, so 30% won't hold. ESPN flags him as a target-gaining slot; even a 20% share is startable. Sleeper from round 10 as a reception-heavy floor play.

travis hunter.verdict: Talented but two-way snaps and poor early efficiency make him a volatile dart, not a floor play.
travis hunter.report: Two-way workload is the whole story: just 7 games of offense-heavy usage, 17.5% target share, WOPR 0.39, negative rec EPA. Low-volume/poor-efficiency as a rookie splitting duties behind Brian Thomas. The ceiling is real if the offense frees him up, but the floor is bleak given defensive snaps and target competition. Volatile dart throw.

makai lemon.verdict: Intriguing rookie profile in a good offense, but hamstring and DeVonta Smith cap a speculative stash.
makai lemon.report: Rookie slot with no NFL data and a Questionable hamstring tag — pure projection. Behind DeVonta Smith in a strong, likely pass-heavier Eagles offense, which is the bull case. Floor is near-zero if the hamstring lingers or targets don't materialize behind Smith and Brown. Speculative bench stash; the profile is intriguing but unproven.

josh downs.verdict: Pittman's absence and red-zone role open real volume for a steady, efficient slot — sleeper value.
josh downs.report: Slot with room to grow: 17.5% target share, 59% snaps in 2025, but 14 red-zone targets and Pittman now out open real volume. Moderate-volume/solid-efficiency (2.27 pts/touch); his rookie-year 70%-snap pace hit ~13 PPG. Ceiling if snap share climbs toward 70%+. Floor capped by Daniel Jones and Alec Pierce. Sleeper worth taking round 10-11 for the opening.

jordan addison.verdict: Boom-bust deep WR2 behind Jefferson; huge air-yards ceiling but capped volume and missed-game risk.
jordan addison.report: Deep-field WR2: aDOT 13.7 and 33% air-yards share drive boom-bust scoring (stdev was 10.5 in 2024). 2024's 213-pt line is the ceiling; 2025 dipped to 135 across 14 games. Low-volume (18%)/good-efficiency but capped behind Jefferson, and added Jauan Jennings competes for looks. A Questionable tag and missed games are the floor risk.

khalil shakir.verdict: Reliable dink-and-dunk PPR volume, but aDOT 3.7 and DJ Moore's arrival limit the ceiling.
khalil shakir.report: Steady PPR slot: 21.1% target share, 72 catches, but aDOT 3.7 and 8.6% air-yards share mean dink-and-dunk volume — high-volume/good-efficiency with a low ceiling. DJ Moore's arrival threatens targets. Reliable floor (stdev 6.0) as a WR4/flex; don't expect spike weeks without deep usage. Value at cost, limited upside.

jayden reed.verdict: Elite per-touch efficiency and Doubs' exit make the healthy ceiling clearly beat ADP — sleeper.
jayden reed.report: Lost 2025 to injury (5-7 games) but 2024 showed elite per-touch juice: 2.63 pts/tgt, 11.6 PPG, plus 20 carries adding rushing. Low-volume/high-efficiency breakout profile if targets return with Doubs gone. A crowded GB room (Watson, Golden) and injury history are the floor risk. Sleeper from round 11 — the efficiency edge and opening beat ADP.

xavier worthy.verdict: Deep, TD-dependent role collapsed with Rice back; upside dart needing an injury ahead of him.
xavier worthy.report: 2025 cratered to 6.5 PPG — just 16.1% target share with Rice back on the field. Deep role (aDOT 12.9) makes him td-dependent and boom-bust. 2024's 187 is the ceiling if Rice misses time. Floor is low given the crowded KC target tree spread by Mahomes. Upside dart, not a floor play.

quentin johnston.verdict: Good volume and efficiency underpriced by the market, though McConkey and TD regression cap upside.
quentin johnston.report: Quietly productive: 20% target share, WOPR 0.50, rec EPA 1.84, 2.01 pts/tgt — good-volume/good-efficiency, though TD-inflated. The market prices him near ADP 143 while a full-board analyst has him WR42; usage backs the higher view. Ladd McConkey and added Tre' Harris cap the ceiling and TD regression is a risk. Solid flex with WR3 upside.

kc concepcion.verdict: Rookie with no data, a camp injury and a buried role behind Jeudy — pure late dart.
kc concepcion.report: Rookie with zero NFL data and a camp injury (left practice early Aug) — speculative. Slot behind Jerry Jeudy in a Browns offense with an unsettled QB room, which caps the ceiling badly. Floor is near-zero if the injury lingers or he stays buried. Late dart only.

deebo samuel.verdict: Dual-threat usage plus a camp opening with SF WRs hurt makes him a sleeper worth the late pick.
deebo samuel.report: Dual-threat volume: 188 PPR pts on 72 catches plus 17 carries in 2025, 72% snaps. Back in SF and camp notes have him getting expanded reps with the other WRs all banged up — a real opening beyond returns. Moderate efficiency, but rushing usage raises both floor and ceiling. Sleeper from round 11 if the SF injuries hold the door open.

chris godwin jr..verdict: Talent intact post-injury and Evans gone; the opportunity and price gap make him a clear sleeper.
chris godwin jr..report: Injury-wrecked 2025 (9 games, 4.9 PPG) but rec EPA 1.63 shows the talent held; he was WR2 overall in 2023. Mike Evans gone and an OC upgrade open volume, and analysts price him well above ADP 145. Low-volume/high-efficiency bounce-back. Injury history is the floor risk. Sleeper from round 11-12 — a clear price and opportunity edge.

romeo doubs.verdict: New England's WR2 with deep efficiency, but a shaky camp keeps him a TD-dependent flyer.
romeo doubs.report: New England's WR2 behind A.J. Brown per beat coverage on a $68M deal. 2025 showed deep efficiency (aDOT 12.8, rec EPA 2.17) — moderate-volume/good-efficiency, TD-reliant. Camp reports have been mixed, opening reps for Boutte, so the WR2 role isn't fully locked. Great offense for receivers if he holds it. Late TD-upside dart.

jayden higgins.verdict: Year-2 breakout with rookie TD efficiency, real camp buzz and expanding role — clear sleeper.
jayden higgins.report: The Year-2 breakout case is loud: 6 TDs matched the WR1 as a rookie on just 12.4% target share (low-volume/good-efficiency), and camp buzz is real — Stroud predicted a dominant year and he's beating Stingley in reps. Opportunity is the swing with Tank Dell competing behind Nico Collins. ESPN breakout call. Sleeper from round 12 — efficiency plus expanding role clearly beat ADP.

jalen coker.verdict: Strong efficiency on thin volume, but WR3 behind McMillan and weak QB play cap the opening.
jalen coker.report: Strong per-target profile: 2.10 pts/tgt, rec EPA 1.99 on a limited 15.4% share — low-volume/high-efficiency. But he's WR3 behind Tetairoa McMillan and Metchie with shaky Bryce Young QB play, so the volume opening is thin. The efficiency intrigues but the depth chart caps it — no sleeper tag until targets clear. Bench flyer.

jerry jeudy.verdict: Big volume, brutal efficiency — the warning quadrant; needs QB help to recover 2024 form.
jerry jeudy.report: Classic warning sign: 20.5% target share and WOPR 0.56 (real volume) but rec EPA/g -1.90 — high-volume/poor-efficiency, the quadrant where the volume itself is at risk. 2024's 241 pts show the ceiling with decent QB play; 2025's Browns QB mess sank him to 7.1 PPG. Decline risk unless the passer improves. Volume-based dart.

rashid shaheed.verdict: Deep-field burner squeezed behind JSN and Kupp; TD-dependent boom-bust bench stash.
rashid shaheed.report: Deep-field burner now in SEA: aDOT 11.4, 22.4% air-yards share — td-dependent boom-bust with negative rec EPA (-0.24). Behind JSN and with Kupp added, his target volume (16.2%) is squeezed. New team, new role. Floor is low, ceiling depends on splash plays. Bench stash.

jalen mcmillan.verdict: Flashed in 2024 but buried behind Egbuka and Godwin; expert sleeper call the depth chart contradicts.
jalen mcmillan.report: 2024 flashed (135 pts, 2.33 pts/tgt) but 2025 was lost to injury (4 games) and he's now WR3 behind Egbuka and Godwin — buried. ESPN and FantasyPros tag him a sleeper on an expanding role, but the depth chart contradicts that with two established WRs ahead. Skipping the sleeper badge — he'd need an injury ahead of him to matter. Deep dart only.

calvin ridley.verdict: Cratered in 2025 and now WR3 in TEN's crowded room — an aging, TD-dependent fade.
calvin ridley.report: Fell off a cliff in 2025: 2.8 PPG over 7 games after 199 pts in 2024. Now WR3 in TEN behind Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale, so the target path is blocked. An age-8 decline plus a crowded room caps both floor and ceiling. Deep aDOT (12.6) makes any value TD-dependent. Late flyer, mostly a fade.
